entities.name: Celia van Schagen
entities.description:
Celia van Schagen was the daughter of Master van Schagen.

For a while past, van Schagen had noticed that his daughter had been visited by a man each night, who had slipped past her tower's security. This led him to believe that the man visiting his daughter was a vampire or a mage. He also was curious that she had red ovular marks on her neck and she seemed in a trance.

When he and Geralt of Rivia were sharing a drink at the Seven Cats Inn in , he asked the witcher to investigate. Later, when the witcher reached the Van Schagen residence, he saw her changing into a dress and walking out onto the balcony. When the witcher followed her, he discovered that the "mysterious man" was Dandelion, who was meeting Celia for a romantic evening. Geralt talked to them and Dandelion showed him a magic trunk of his that had teleported him to the tower they were in. He read the runes inside and the trunk flew off with Geralt and him inside it, leaving Celia on the balcony.

entities.name: Chireadan
entities.description:
Chireadan was an elf from the Redanian city of Rinde, a tavern owner, and Errdil's cousin.

Despite elves typically not finding humans to be attractive, he was secretly in love with Yennefer, though he never revealed his feelings to the sorceress. However, he didn't let his feelings get in the way when he saw that Geralt was also infatuated with Yennefer and even pulled the others away when he saw the two having sex in his cousin's destroyed inn after fighting off a djinn.

In Chapter IV, at the Lakeside, Chireadan, an elf among Toruviel's ragtag group recognizes Geralt. It seems he knows the witcher from somewhere before, but of course Geralt has no memory of him. This previous encounter, which is not described in any further detail, is a reference to the The Last Wish.

He is also a sharper, and thus one of the available dice players. He can be found any time, day or night to play. During the day, he is typically sitting at one of the two campfires nearest the Elven Cave. At night, he will be sleeping in the cave, but does not complain at all about being woken up just for a game.

entities.name: Colm Coimeádaí
entities.description:
Colm Coimeádaí was the leader of a guerrilla force in the forests of Ekerot's isle that fought for animal and monster rights sometime during the . He was highly skilled in unarmed combat, despite missing his right arm.

Born to a fisherman from an unknown place, Colm's father and mother, while she was pregnant with him, set off on his father's boat for a better life. The winds blew them to an island somewhere in the North Sea, and for several nights they had peace. This ended, however, when Colm's father was killed by wolves while hunting, and his mother dying weeks later during childbirth, leaving the newborn Colm alone in the wilderness. Animals, or monsters according to some, took him in and raised him as their own. Slowly he found an abandoned fort and began gaining followers from nearby villagers, men and women similarly minded with their care for animal rights.

After not long this mindset started to become violent and two-sided, Colm's men captured the local man Strandmark's milkmaid wife and cut her breasts off (as she would cut the cow's udders off after they were finished producing), shod a blacksmith's feet like a horse until he bled to death, drowned the fisherman Thulin (as he would cut off the fins and tails of the fish and release them out of cruelty), beheaded the henkeeper Pavlo (as he was cutting off his hen's feathers to cram more into their coop), and let wolves in to eat the tanner Inga in her home.

Around a week later, Colm and his warriors observed a local woman Ingma and her daughter Berit torturing elderly wolves, and later killing a group while rescuing the witcher Geralt of Rivia, who impressed Colm with his attempt to prevent the creature's deaths. The guerrilla leader ordered his men to kill the mother and capture the daughter and Geralt, before returning to their settlement. Not long after returning, Geralt was brought to him and the two walked through the forest, discussing the moralities of killing a human versus an animal. After a short while, they came across a pack of drowners, and Geralt, instinctively from years of killing them, drew his sword. Colm though quickly calmed the witcher, explaining they were safe if they continued without fear, which worked and they returned to the settlement. There, the two ate lunch and Colm urged Geralt to help him kill the local Jarl Ekerot who was torturing drowners, though Geralt refused on moral grounds. In response, Colm had Berit brought out and used as blackmail to convince the witcher to agree to the deal.

Dayo was an Ofieri woman that, along with Ameena, Dandelion slept with in , after he was teleported to Ofir. They discussed Radeyah, the crown sorceress.

They later had a meeting with Phyre, where Dandelion asked whether he could perform for Nibras, to which the eunuch replied that it would be difficult.

Later Dayo went looking for proof of Maraal and Zaira's relationship where she was stopped by Ameena, but Dayo went on into a room where she happened upon something shocking. ru:Дайо Category:Humans Category:Characters in the comics

entities.name: Drugan
entities.description:
Drugan was a Nilfgaardian captain who was stationed alongside his company in the village of Vorune in No Man's Land (more commonly known as Velen). He and his men were terrorising the hamlet and subjugating its residents when Geralt and Vesemir passed through during their search for Yennefer. Their actions were met with Geralt's disapproval, but Vesemir was swift to remind him that such behaviour was not uncommon during periods of conflict. Nevertheless, the duo stayed in the village a while after hearing tell of a fiend that had been plaguing the local area.

The final straw came when Drugan and his company executed several of the villagers, including the boy Baltt who had aided the two witchers in their investigations. Geralt and Vesemir led Drugan and his men to the last known location of the fiend and, by way of a rare herb known to attract the creatures, baited the fiend into attacking the captain and his company. Drugan was torn apart by it whilst the witchers ruminated on how nothing forces them to stop two monsters from killing one another.

entities.description:
Dziega was an assimilated vran in Blaviken.

Dziega liked to drink beer near a stall at the town square with a werebbubb friend. He or she tried not to interfere in human affairs and felt antipathy towards people who were trying to cadge free drinks, to which she included Dandelion.

In the 1230s, during the famed Butchering, Dziega stood amongst the crowd of onlookers trying to dissuade the werebbubb friend from commenting, in fear that humans would be angry for weighing in and kill him.

entities.name: Dziega's friend
entities.description:
The friend of Dziega was an assimilated werebbubb in Blaviken.

In the 1230s, the werebbubb was drinking beer with his vran friend when Dandelion came and asked if he could join. Although Dziega disagreed, the werebbubb poured a goblet for the bard to "support art". As a sign of gratitude, Dandelion promised to write about the werebbubb's generosity in one of his ballads.

Moments later, the infamous butchering ensued. The werebbubb stood in the crowd of onlookers with Dandelion and Dziega, latter of which warned him to not comment, afraid nearby humans would get mad at the werebbubb for weighing in and behead him. Believing Renfri's band, outnumbering Geralt of Rivia six to one, would defeat a witcher, the werebbubb was utterly surprised when Geralt won.

entities.name: Eggar
entities.description:
Eggar was a Vergeni dwarf from the Free Realm of Upper Aedirn.

In Eggar traveled to Vergen with his fellow dwarf, Barclay Els, where they were celebrated by the locals and tasked by Saskia to kill a chelonodrake. Joining the two dwarfs were Yarpen Zigrin, Maevarienn and Geralt of Rivia, as well as Saskia.

The company rode to a nearby marsh, just after a nasty encounter with a pack of nekkers. At the marsh they found the chelonodrake in a nearby lake, next to a group of drowners. During the fight with the drowners, one struck Eggar in the back, though he did survive, just before the group quickly killed the rest of them. He survived the fight with the chelondrake, but then left the company.

entities.name: Ekerot
entities.description:
Ekerot was a jarl of an isle during the .

Around the time of his son's fourth birthday, the jarl began to notice a disturbing perpetuity for his son to bring in animal corpses and torture them. A year later, an axe was requested and used within the week to violently kill a cow to watch for its reaction. Knowing his son was becoming a psychopath and with no end in sight, the jarl agreed to provide monsters such as drowners for his son to torture and kill. From then, his own bloodlust grew, and he began weekly hunts in which he left his guards near the edge of the woods and hunted a great manner of beasts alone, such as bears to "satiate his bloodlust" according to many.

Sometime later, a guerrilla clan known for viewing all animals as equals formed in the woods near Ekerot's settlement, and he began a long-term campaign to round them up and execute them, bolstered by a reward he offered to the locals for assistance.

Soon after, while in the process of a hunt, he was ambushed by a pack of drowners and quickly overwhelmed. As he screamed to his guards for assistance, the witcher Geralt of Rivia arrived and swiftly held them off, as well as helped Ekerot return to his guards. As a thanks, the jarl invited the witcher to dinner with himself and his son, which quickly turned into a dispute between the two family members when Ekerot had no explanation for his wife's disappearance for their child, and so after, when the two were left to talk, Ekerot told Geralt of Colm Coimeádaí, the leader of the "bandit" guerrilla camp. The witcher disagreed to hunting Colm down though, due to the morality of hunting intelligent beings.

Elid was the young son of Ostrit and his one night stand, Maerlina, who lived in Novigrad. His arm grew feathers and he had ability to change into a crow, meaning he either could polymorph, or he was under some sort of spell. He tried to live an honorable way, not drinking and not looking at women, until Geralt brought him to the tavern.

entities.name: Elisa
entities.description:
Elisa (Polish: Eliza) was one of two children born to Maerlina and Ostrit, though she and her brother, Elid, never knew their father when he was alive. However, through a series of events, she was consumed by rage and hatred, cursing her to take on a monstrous form. She then used this form to kill others, believing she was getting revenge for all the injustice done to her.

Not much is known about her childhood, though she never knew her father as her mother had left Vizima when the striga attacks started.

After her mother left Vizima and wandered the world, the Third Northern War started. Believing her children would be safer away from any major settlements while fighting broke out, Maerlina sent Elisa and Elid to live with their grandmother in Velen. However, the war spread here too, and the village dealt with a constant food shortage. While the villagers shared meager bits of food amongst each other, like half rotten vegetables, none shared outside of their own families any meat they managed to hunt down, and many fought over the smallest scraps they could find.

At one point their grandmother became ill, and Elisa and Elid struggled to take care of her and themselves, when Elisa spotted a wounded Nilfgaardian soldier pass through. When she asked where he came from, he told her from a battlefield west of the village. Seizing on this information that could lead to food, Elisa quickly grabbed her brother and took off for the battlefield in question, where sure enough many lay dead. While Elid was reluctant to disturb a place where many died, Elisa quickly set to work and her brother soon followed suit.

entities.name: Elivalla
entities.description:
Elivalla was a mercenary hired by Rensor Bolius to help in claiming Corvo Bianco.

Elivalla was a member of Clentaest's mercenary group. During their jobs, Clentaest had saved his life hundreds of times. They were hired by a man claiming to be Lord Rensor Bolius to assist him in reclaiming the Corvo Bianco estate from Geralt of Rivia. Together with the group, Elivalla approached the estate at night after witnessing Yennefer of Vengerberg arrive for a visit.

The next day, they met up with Lord Bolius at the Beauclair market, where one of the group challenged Elivalla to down an entire pint in one go, which he then did. Later that morning, the group went to confront Geralt and Yennefer at Corvo Bianco, stating that Lord Bolius wanted his estate back. They then accompanied Bolius and Geralt to Duchess Anna Henrietta, but were dismissed by Bolius after he learned Geralt was a witcher.

The next day, Elivalla and Clentaest went with Geralt to free a prisoner named Black-Eyed Benno, who had information about Lord Bolius's son. At first, Elivalla mocked Geralt, but was told to stop by Clentaest. While Clentaest and Geralt talked, Elivalla kept watch and alerted the pair when the prisoner transfer passed by. During the assault, Geralt used Aard to blast Clentaest off her horse. Elivalla was angered by this, but Geralt told him to handle the other guard on horseback. The dwarf caught up with the rider and jumped off his horse to push the other rider off.

entities.name: Eltibald
entities.description:
Eltibald was a mage known for his investigations into the Curse of the Black Sun.

Eltibald investigated menhirs erected by the Dauk and tombstones in Wozgor necropolises, and familiarized himself with the bobolaks' mythology, and came to the conclusion that a certain solar eclipse, known as the Black Sun, would transform sixty of the girls born under it into cruel creatures who, ultimately, would bring about the return of the goddess Lilit and the end of the world.

Because of this idea, girls born of this curse, of all social classes, from peasants to royals, were hunted down by certain mages. Some were killed and others were locked away in high towers, while others were subjected to autopsy, and at least one to vivisection.

Later, after Maraal was killed by Geralt, he took the rank of crown assassin.

entities.name: Eyck of Denesle
entities.description:
Eyck of Denesle was a pious, virtuous, flawless, and spotless knight (except for being highly prejudiced against witchers, sorcerers, and nonhumans, and fanatical in his faith), who has killed manticores and griffins in the past, as well as dragons. However, as he saw it as a civic duty to purge the world of abominations, he doesn't accept money for his slayings, making him competition for witchers like Geralt of Rivia.

Eyck went to Hołopole after a summons went out for a dragon-slayer as did many other potential trophy hunters.

When an avalanche hit the band of would-be dragon-slayers, Eyck helped Dandelion save Geralt and Yennefer who nearly went over the edge and were very close to falling to their deaths, not to mention arguing. Once he had saved them, though, he demanded that the king "clear the ranks of the filth", including Geralt and Yennefer.

He challenged Villentretenmerth like the good knight he was and the dragon knocked him off his horse with the most effortless flick of its tail, damaging his spine and legs.

She came up with the idea of scaring away unwanted visitors by riding on galloping Nivellen's back, completely naked and blowing the hunting horn of Nivellen's grandfather.

entities.name: Foltest
entities.description:
Foltest was the king of Temeria, prince of Sodden, sovereign of Pontaria and Mahakam as well as the senior protector of Brugge and Ellander. He was the son of King Medell and Queen Sancia of Sodden, making him a member of the Temerian Dynasty.

Sancia's royal connection with Sodden turned the principality into a vassal state and Ekkehard began paying tribute to Temeria after the death of Gutram. The king's Royal Council in Vizima included the sorceresses Triss Merigold and Keira Metz, as well as Fercart of Cidaris, Willemer the priest, Bronibor and Hereward of Ellander.

While still a young prince, Foltest and his cousin Jurkast often travelled through the countryside to have fun with willing women. During one such expedition, they lost themselves near Brokilon. After a whole day of wandering through dense forest they found a glade with a hut in the center, encircled by dryads. They ushered the princes inside where two chosen dryads slept with them in order to have children. When the princes woke up in the morning, they were accompanied by two dryads whose task was to lead them out of Brokilon safely.

Foltest was a wise and handsome monarch. As with his predecessor, he was not fond of his grandfather, Hugo of Rivia. Upon his accession to the Temerian throne, he demanded that Hugo's portrait be removed from the throne room and had a habit of "leaving Hugo out" of the family genealogy. Foltest devoted plenty of time to lauding his great-grandfather, Griffin, as he was known to speak warmly of "Grandmama Bienvenu" and "Great-grandmama Clarissa". He tended to be highly evasive of any questions regarding family lineage.

entities.name: Forst Bolin
entities.description:
Forst Bolin was a doppler who ran a hostel, but only so he could murder and rob patrons. When the townspeople began to realize what he was doing, he quickly ran away and a bounty was put out for him to be brought in alive so he could be tried for his crimes.

In his attempt to escape, he took on the guise of a young woman, Jayne. However, this proved to not work in his favor as a troll in the area, Rockstride, caught the doppler and began to take "her" back to his home, believing that Jayne would dance for his wife and make her happy and not yell anymore.

Fortunately for Forst, Geralt and Ciri were traveling through on their way to Novigrad and saw what was happening. Geralt stepped in and persuaded the troll to release his captive and Forst, staying in his Jayne disguise, took up Ciri's offer to tag along with them to Novigrad.

That night, when asked about her past, Jayne explained she grew up outside Mulbrydale but found village life boring and eventually rode off to see the world. After they all went to sleep though, a werewolf snuck up and grabbed Geralt's swords and Jayne, intending to kill all of them. However, it hadn't noticed Ciri had been hiding, and the witchers quickly dispatched of the werewolf with Jayne only surprised at having another monster encounter.

entities.name: Frank
entities.description:
Frank was a witcher from the School of the Wolf.

Frank was one of the Wolf School witchers who participated in the Witcher Tournament. Before the tournament, he was among the wolves who traveled to Devil's Cliff after the sorceresses underwent their transformation on the night of Belleteyn. Although he initially didn't have a companion for the evening, he was approached by the elf Fionnuala, and they slipped away into the bushes for some private time together.

During the Trial of Forest Eyes, Frank, like several other witchers, cheated by removing his blindfold. As punishment, Vesemir hung them upside down by their ankles as a reprimand.

During the tournament, the School of the Cat sprang their trap under the orders of King Radowit II's royal astrologer, Astrogarus. However, the Cats were betrayed by the king, and Frank, along with the other Wolf and Cat witchers present, was killed. Only Geralt of Rivia survived.

entities.name: Fredefalk Vellga
entities.description:
Fredefalk or Friedfalk Vellga was prince of Creyden and the father of Renfri. He married Aridea after the demise of his first wife Silvena, Renfri's mother.

Not much is known about Fredefalk except with his first wife he had a daughter named Renfri, whom he adored. After his first wife presumably died, he started a relationship with Aridea, with whom he had a couple children out of wedlock before the two married. It's known they had at least one son while they were together. However, years later, Aridea was poisoned and subsequently died and rumors spread that Fredefalk himself killed her after finding a younger, more robust, mistress. He shortly died himself in a strange hunting accident.

entities.name: Fregenal
entities.description:
Fregenal was once an elder druid from the Mayena Circle of Druids before he was expelled eleven years prior to the events of the short story "Droga, z której się nie wraca".

The circumstances under which he was expelled remain unknown, but before leaving, Fregenal stole several pages from forbidden books. With these pages, he studied the dangerous magic of the wizard Alzur.

He reportedly used this magic to create the first koshchey by using Alzur's Double Cross (though it also could have been caused by some other spell), and formed the band of mercenaries known as Koshchey's Men. Fregenal and Koshchey's Men began terrorising villages in the Amell Mountains, robbing them, raping their women, and in some cases murdering the villagers and razing the villages to the ground.

In one such village, the mountainside Klucz, a blacksmith named Mikula began rallying the villages to oppose Fregenal and his mercenaries, but he required more aid. After being rebuffed by the militia of Mayena, Mikula appealed to the circle of druids there for support. Fregenal learnt of the blacksmith's schemes and dispatched a witch in his employ, Manissa, to assassinate the druid at the crossroads to Klucz. His ploy failed when fate intervened and the warrior Korin arrived at the crossroads instead. The druidess Visenna arrived shortly thereafter, and she and Korin joined forces with Mikula's assembled force at Klucz. Meanwhile, after learning that Fregenal was bent on world domination, a werebbubb by the name of Kehl led a revolt against the renegade sorcerer over their conflicting goals, capturing the druid and leaving him for the oncoming army.

Gar (Polish: Niszczuka) was one of the Crinfrid Reavers, a group of mercenaries hired by King Niedamir to take part in the hunt for Myrgtabrakke, a green dragon outside Barefield. He was older than Kennet, but younger than Boholt, their leader. He had a preference for wielding a large two-handed sword..

Sometime around , he and Kennet took the first apprentice, Newboy. A few years afterward, the Reavers grew in numbers with Gar, Boholt, Kennet and, to some extent, Newboy remembered as legends.

entities.name: Gardis
entities.description:
Gardis was a witcher and a student of the School of the Wolf. He was one of the witchers who participated in the Witcher Tournament.

Gardis was trained as a witcher at the School of the Wolf. When the Wolf and Cat schools were ordered by King Radowit II to engage in emotional integration measures and exam, Gardis was among the witchers chosen for an exchange. He traveled alongside Aubry, Geralt, and Gweld. During their journey, Gardis teased Gweld for his sensitive nature.

At the exchange, tensions began to rise between Geralt, Gweld, and the Cat witchers. Gardis tried to deescalate the situation, reminding Geralt that they weren't supposed to fight. When a duel between Gweld and the Cat witcher "Mouse Hunter" threatened to spiral out of control, a group of locals arrived, but Vesemir and Guxart intervened just in time, restoring order. It was decided that only Gweld would be exchanged, while the others returned to their respective camps.

Later, during the Trial of Forest Eyes, Gardis, like most of the other Wolf witchers, cheated by removing his blindfold. As punishment, Vesemir hung them upside down by their ankles.

entities.name: Giltine
entities.description:
Giltine was a Redanian woman and the daughter of Potrim and Juna who lived in Neisse during the .

Throughout her childhood, Giltine was assaulted and groomed by her father who valued her more than his wife Juna. At a certain point in her teenage years, she fell pregnant with his child, and so her father hired a lamia working nearby to help terminate the birth. Traumatised by this and her youth, Giltine soon after heard a traveler tell Potrim of two witches in the Kestrel Mountains that could help with emotions and so she fled to their mountainous retreat. The two witches, Milda and Zemyna, began teaching the group that had gathered, including Giltine, about the five stages of a true lament - exordium, laudatio, comploratio, consolatio, exhortatio.

A short while later, following Potrim's wishes, the witcher Geralt of Rivia arrived at the retreat to convince Giltine to come home, having been told by her father she had been kidnapped. Controlled by her desire to heal her grief, Giltine refused to go, stating she would rather slit her wrists than return in that pain. The following day, the group met to continue their tutelage, joined by Geralt, and before he was attacked by member Bandura, Giltine admitted her pregnancy and termination, much to the witcher's surprise. Finally, during the night, he was able to convince her to leave the retreat as her admission had helped her heal.

After returning to her family manor, Giltine was reunited with her father and mother, the latter becoming so overjoyed and mentally broken that she randomly bit Potrim's nose. As night fell, Giltine took her revenge for years of abuse, cutting her father's throat with a sword while her mother could only watch blankly, her mind almost completely gone. As the witcher burst in, the lamia that had assisted Giltine possessed her and called for the guards, blaming Potrim's death on Geralt. As Giltine was now lady of the manor, they followed her orders, knocking him to the ground and only holding off killing him on Giltine's, or technically the lamia's, orders. Geralt was strapped to a chair where he awoke to Giltine and Juna explaining the lamia's motivations, before Giltine left, burning Neisse as she went until she arrived at Agobard's house. As she explained her reasoning for Agobard's coming execution, Geralt ran over, having been let free by Juna, and killed the guards and knocked out Giltine.

When Nivellen was first afflicted with the curse which turned him into a "monster in a monster's skin", no one, including Nivellen, knew what was happening and Glutton ran away from the beast that had replaced her master when he attacked his staff. A family parrot also simply died of fright at the sight of the transformed youth. Luckily for Nivellen, Glutton came back to his manor and for a time was his only companion.

entities.name: Guxart
entities.description:
Guxart was a witcher from the School of the Cat and served as the right-hand man of the School's leader, Treyse.

When the Dyn Marv caravan was stationed in Kaedwen under the sponsorship of King Radowit II, the Schools of the Cat and Wolf were ordered to engage in emotional integration measures. However, both schools only halfheartedly participated. Later, a Witcher Tournament was organized between the two schools, intended to determine which would continue to receive royal funding and gain the exclusive right to operate in Kaedwen.

Guxart oversaw the training at the Cat School's camp in preparation for the tournament. During the student exchange at an inn, tensions flared and led to a duel. Guxart, along with Vesemir, intervened just in time to prevent it from escalating into a full-blown brawl. Although Guxart didn't particularly like Vesemir, the two witchers agreed to exchange only the student Gweld and send the others back. Both men found the situation suspicious and suspected someone might be trying to pit the two schools against each other.

Back at the Cat School camp, Guxart was deeply impressed with Gweld's swordsmanship, eventually running out of worthy opponents for him to face. Unbeknownst to Guxart, his deputy was secretly training the Cat witchers in wrestling under the orders of the royal astrologer, Astrogarus.
entities.short_description: Guxart was a witcher from the School of the Cat and served as the right-hand man of the School's leader, Treyse.

entities.name: Gweld
entities.description:
Gweld was a witcher from the School of the Wolf and a close friend of Geralt of Rivia during their training.

Gweld was brought to Kaer Morhen to undergo training and the mutations required to become a witcher. During his time there, he developed a strong bond with fellow trainee Geralt. Both underwent the grueling Witcher Trials, one of which involved blocking incoming crossbow bolts with their swords. The experience left a lasting impact on Gweld, who later suffered nightmares about his training and the mutation process.

Later, Gweld and Geralt were among the group of Wolf students chosen to participate in an exam organized by King Radowit II of Kaedwen. The exam was designed as a Witcher Tournament between the Wolf School and the School of the Cat. As part of the arrangements, the schools were also ordered to exchange students, and Gweld was selected for the exchange.

At the inn where the exchange was to take place, Gweld and Geralt swapped medallions as a symbol of their friendship. This act, noticed by the Cat witchers, drew mockery from them, particularly from a Cat witcher Gweld derisively nicknamed "Mouse Hunter" and "Mouse-Eater." The tension escalated into a duel between Gweld and the Cat witcher. Gweld's superior swordsmanship allowed him to win easily, but before the situation could deteriorate further, a group of local peasants arrived. The Cats lied to the locals, accusing the Wolves of provoking the fight. The situation was defused only when Vesemir and Guxart intervened. Following this, it was decided that Gweld would stay at the Cat School while the other Wolves returned to their camp.
entities.short_description: Gweld was a witcher from the School of the Wolf and a close friend of Geralt of Rivia during their training.

entities.name: Gwen
entities.description:
Gwen was a witcher of the School of the Wolf who trained under Vesemir.

During his training alongside fellow trainees Geralt, Gweld, and Hemminks, Gwen participated in a training exercise led by Vesemir. In this exercise, blunt crossbow bolts were fired at the witchers to teach them how to parry the bolts with their swords. Unfortunately, both Gwen and Hemminks failed to block the bolts and were hit. When they were being prepared to be taken to the infirmary for treatment, one of the witchers remarked that Gwen might need to be taken directly to the sand for burial, as he had been struck in the eye by a bolt.

entities.name: Hemminks
entities.description:
Hemminks was a witcher from the School of the Wolf and trained under Vesemir.

Hemminks was a witcher of the School of the Wolf. One day, during a training session alongside Geralt, Gweld, and Gwen, they were tasked with blocking incoming crossbow bolts as part of their swordsmanship training. While Hemminks and Gwen both failed to block the bolts, Hemminks was sent to the infirmary for treatment.

Hemminks later participated in the Witcher Tournament. Prior to the tournament, the Wolf School witchers underwent the Trial of Forest Eyes, during which all except Geralt cheated by removing their blindfolds. As punishment, Vesemir hung them upside down by their ankles.

On the day of the tournament, Hemminks was paired against fellow Wolf witcher Gardis. However, the Cat School witchers sprang their trap under orders from the royal astrologer, Astrogarus. In a turn of events, King Radowit II betrayed the Cat witchers and ordered the execution of all witchers present. Hemminks died alongside the others, with Geralt being the only survivor.

entities.name: Hurgan Bolt
entities.description:
Hurgan Bolt was a dwarf who lived in Malleore and a blacksmith. He was also the Elder of the Lumberjack's Guild in Creigiau.

During Geralt's stay in Creigiau Castle, he was introduced to Hurgan by Lazare, the castle's castellan. The witcher and the dwarf discussed the local leshy that had been terrorising the local area. The two traveled together to nearby ruins where the leshy had been spotted, where Hurgan left the witcher.

Later when Anton de Creigiau attacked the castle, Hurgan and Geralt fought side by side killing the werecats. But while Anton was charging at Lady Sérlait, Hurgan got in his way and Anton slit his throat.

She came to Nivellen shortly after Primula. Like the two before her, Ilka was first afraid of him but then, after receiving good treatment and gifts, became aroused. After a year, she left rich and with tender farewells.

At some point, as revenge for her making a profit off animal hides, Colm Coimeádaí's men let wolves into her hut who ate her to death.

entities.name: Ingma
entities.description:
Ingma was a hunter and fur trader who lived with her daughter Berit in the forests of Ekerot's isle sometime in the .

She was a keen hunter, though was cruel; Ingma would capture the older wolves and snare them together, starving the creatures until they had no option except to kill each other to eat. At some point, her and her daughter happened upon the witcher Geralt of Rivia being attacked by a pack of wolves on the shores of the isle while hunting. As Ingma was hunting the beasts regardless for their pelts, she shot them with her bow and carried the witcher to refuge in their family home.

After cauterising his wounds and preparing food, Ingma in the morning sent Berit on horseback to inform Jarl Ekerot of the witcher's arrival and sat down with Geralt for a meal. As she mentioned the guerrilla gang formed in the local woods, to which Geralt mentioned he'd seen a masked possible accomplice on the way, Ingma became startled, yelling they were being watched. As she instructed the witcher to grab his sword to protect them from a possible attack, she was shot through the back of the throat by one of the guerrilla fighters; one of Colm Coimeádaí's men.

entities.name: Jakob Ornstine
entities.description:
Jakob Ornstine was a hunter that Geralt met on the edge of Caed Dhu in Angren.

When he was 10 years old, he first met Marta on account of her walking through town to sell her mother's baked goods. At the time, Jakob would follow her about as he was wanting the pastries she was selling, Over time though, as the two grew up, he became infatuated with her, but she had no feelings for him. Instead of accepting this, Jakob instead got her father to sell her into marriage to him for 21 silver coins and seven fox skins.

Their marriage from the start was abusive, with Jakob forcing himself on her and beating her regularly, all while saying it was love. He also didn't appear to accept the reality, and instead invented an idealized relationship in his head, where they were happy and led a wonderful life together, a far cry from reality. Then one day, after he crushed a few of Marta's prized seashells she'd collected, he sent her to the blacksmith, Talton, to create a new dagger with an inlaid hilt.

Jakob began to get suspicious when Marta was frequently checking on the dagger's progress and, about three weeks after putting in the request, he caught Talton and Marta having a rendezvous on the beach. Angry over this, he killed Talton, but Jakob started to believe that instead of him killing another person, he had instead saved his wife from a horrible sea monster that almost dragged her into the sea and the marks on her body were from the vicious ordeal rather than love marks Talton had left behind on Marta. He also began to believe Marta was a bruxa and drained him of his manhood and some time later, he killed her, but not before she cursed his very existence.

Javil Fysh was a merchant and the associate and partner of Petru Cobbin. He met the witcher Geralt and the dwarf Addario Bach when the duo where asked to escort the cutter, the Prophet Lebioda, on its voyage. The vessel was hunted by an Aguara as it was holding its offspring, and whilst attempting to escape from the creature Javil was torn apart by a crocodile and a turtle.

entities.name: Jean-Christophe de Bourbeau
entities.description:
Jean-Christophe de Bourbeau was the owner of the Tufo vineyard. He was married to Andrée de Bourbeau and expected those of lower social status to refer to him with deference.

Jean-Christophe ran the Tufo vineyard. Several years before , his vineyard suffered from tremors that caused the buildings to shake—one even collapsed. He put out a contract for anyone to investigate. Eventually, the witcher Junod of Belhaven accepted the contract, but he was never seen or heard from again.

Then in , the vineyard once again began suffering from tremors, and now people were also going missing, the latest being Jean-Luc. Jean-Christophe put out a contract again, this time offering it to any knight who could find and slay whatever was causing the tremors.

Despite their initial meeting, Jean-Christophe and Geralt developed a friendship. He visited the witcher's estate of Corvo Bianco with gifts of wine. On one such visit, he and Geralt discussed wine and what it takes to make a good vintage over food and drink. Jean-Christophe then asked Geralt to handle some monsters ravaging his vineyard; in return, he gifted the witcher twenty bottles of his wine. Some days later, he visited Geralt again while Corvo Bianco was being repaired from fire damage. He tried Geralt's latest batch of wine and congratulated him, saying it was far above average. Noticing that, despite his improved wine, Geralt was sad, Jean-Christophe asked why. When Geralt said that maybe his wine needed sadness, Jean-Christophe proposed they drink to sadness. After explaining why only wine truly matters in the end, he asked Geralt what he would name his wine.

entities.name: Joachim Schwann's daughter
entities.description:
She was the unnamed daughter of the tax collector of Novigrad, Joachim Schwann, and his wife Lady Schwann.

After Joachim's death, she began a line of promiscuity and so her mother paid a mage to cast a spell that would teach her to save it for marriage: anyone she kissed would be transformed into a frog.

In , after folk spread word of a monster transforming noblewomen into frogs around the city due to her curse, the witcher Geralt of Rivia found one of the hybrid frog-men Joachim's daughter had tricked, kissed and transformed in the sewers. The witcher fought the creature, who told him Schwann's daughter was the actual one with the curse, and so Geralt confronted the mother and daughter and convinced them to reconcile and reenlist the mage's help in removing the curse.

entities.name: Jula
entities.description:
Jula was a Skelliger woman who lived on an unknown isle during the .

After her mother's pigs were stolen by an unknown entity, Jula and a fellow warrior tracked it through the woods near their village. They quickly found her mother, the witcher Geralt of Rivia, and a nekker. As it was revealed the nekker was responsible for the pig's disappearance and Geralt was hesitant to kill it due to the creature's timid nature, Jula stated she would kill him too if the witcher got in the way of her hunt. Seemingly from nowhere, the nomadic mage Paco Barbloes appeared, also wishing to be the one to slay the beast. As they got locked into a standoff and the pig suddenly squealed, Jula's partner shot his crossbow out of fright, the bolt piercing right through Paco's neck and causing him to shoot a fireball at Jula's head and explode it in flames.

entities.name: Juna
entities.description:
Juna was a lady of Gelibol during the and the wife of Potrim.

After her daughter Giltine fled to the Kestrel Mountains for a lament, Juna went mad, believing Giltine had been kidnapped by the same witches aiding her sorrow, even going as far as becoming suicidal and randomly attacking Potrim.

Not long after, the witcher Geralt of Rivia arrived in Neisse and nearby in the woods found a group of water hags about to attack Juna. After he saved her, the witcher and Agobard returned Juna to her husband, and set off in search of Giltine. After returning a while later with the young girl, Juna became overjoyed to have her daughter back and randomly attacked Potrim again, this time biting his nose. As her mental health had deteriorated so far, Juna that evening stood by as Giltine killed her father for the years of sexual abuse he had inflicted on her. Moments later, Geralt burst into the room looking for Potrim to confront him about the abuse, and so Giltine, concurrently possessed by a lamia, called for the house guards, stating the witcher had killed her father. After Geralt got knocked out in a fight with them, he awoke tied-up to Giltine and Juna alone with him and the three unfolded the events and their moralities, ending with the possessed Giltine stating she would not stop and she would kill the men in all of Gelibol if needed to teach them respect for women.

As Giltine went to confront Agobard, Geralt managed to convince Juna to untie him under one reasoning: she could have her revenge but save her daughter by letting herself be tied-up, possessed, and then killed by him as the lamia's final host, this being her demise hours later when the lamia possessed her attempting to get back to Giltine.

When the witcher Geralt of Rivia came to their mountainous retreat to take back one of the lament group, Giltine, to her father, Kagan was stuck in the fourth stage of his lament: comploratio, otherwise known as the stage of mourning. He witnessed the fight break out between the witcher and group member Bandura, and stayed for the witches' help following Giltine's leave.

entities.description:
Karl Grimm was a Temerian miner and member of the Grimm family.

After receiving funding from the Hogge sisters to capitalise on a copper mine, Karl, and his sons Kurt and Kopek, constructed the venture at the future site of Grimmwald, the town he built from the ore's profits. Fortifying an impressive wealth, the veins eventually ran dry, and Karl realised he had lost nearly everything, his life too. He left his two sons a mountain of debt, but before he died, he started selling off his assets, trying to facilitate and maintain his lavish life for its brief remainder.

entities.name: Kehl
entities.description:
Kehl was a mercenary and, for a short time, leader of the Koshchey's Men.

Kehl was a long-time mercenary who gained much experience over his life.

At one point in the 12th century, he joined the band formed by renegade druid Fregenal. They became feared in the settlements of Klamat pass. After realizing their differing intentions, Kehl and seventeen other members of the band turned on their leader. They killed the rest and left tied Fregenal in a cave. Kehl became a new leader and decided to leave the area for good.

Later, Kehl returned to aid Visenna and Korin kill the koshchey summoned by Fregenal. He rode against the abomination with warcry, sword in hand. Koshchey grabbed Kehl's horse and threw it away but the brave werebbubb swooped under it and stabbed the monster in one of its limbs. Angry and wounded, koshchey picked Kehl from the ground and massacred him.

entities.description:
Kennet was the youngest member of the original three Crinfrid Reavers, a group of mercenaries hired by King Niedamir to take part in the hunt for, Myrgtabrakke a dragon outside Barefield. He was known for his expertise with a two-handed sword. He fought alongside Gar and Boholt, their leader. By the time of 1271, Kennet has seemingly become the leader of the Reavers and addressed Geralt outside Foltest's army camp. A few years afterward, the Reavers grew in numbers with Kennet, Boholt, Gar and, to some extent, Newboy remembered as quite a legends.

entities.name: Kopek Grimm
entities.description:
Kopek Grimm was a therianthrope and member of the Grimm family that resided in Grimmwald.

His father Karl was a miner who opened a copper mine near the eventual site of the town, which he constructed with Kopek and his brother Kurt's help with the massive funds generated from the ore veins. Eventually, as the ore ran dry, their father began to swindle away, drinking and whoring his way into an early grave, meanwhile spending all of the family fortune trying to continue his lavish life. Before his death, he sold Grimmwald to the Hogge sisters; Kurt, angered deeply by his father's descent and the loss of the town, took Kopek and condemned the sisters beginning a life for the two as bandits, robbing and raiding on the road.

During this period, Kurt tried to keep his younger brother from seeing the horrors the men committed, such as rape or murder, though it still scarred Kopek deeply. Eventually, at a temple near Mirt, the gang assaulted a priestess who cursed them all as she killed herself. A few days later, the group were turned into lycanthropes: Kopek into a weredog, and his brother a werewolf. Kopek, hurt by this process, returned to Grimmwald to become a servant for the Hogges.

At some point afterward, the witcher Geralt of Rivia and his friend Dandelion came into town, where Kopek saw them talking of a werewolf problem and asking for leads. As he went to approach them, however, Red took their attention for her lead, and so he left. Later, he led them to their rooms and explained who he was, and that it was his brother who was the werewolf they were looking for. After a while of their searching, and strain from pretending to make peace with reality, Kopek killed Lea Hogge in his dog form while she slept. The following day, they all came to the manor and after being exposed as Lea's killer and getting into a fight with his brother, Brooke Hogge shot Kopek through the back of the throat with a crossbow.

He was a wanderer, churl, troublemaker, and swashbuckler. While Korin was not present in his life, Geralt believed his father's genes were more dominant, evidenced by his own proficiency at "swashing a buckler".

He knows a secret tempel language, which enable him to translate for Geralt the 'exorcism', the latter had used against a djinn.

entities.name: Kurt Grimm
entities.description:
Kurt Grimm was a lycanthrope and member of the Grimm family that resided in Grimmwald.

His father Karl was a miner who opened a copper mine near the eventual site of the town, which he constructed with Kurt and his brother Kopek's help with the massive funds generated from the ore veins. Eventually, as the ore ran dry, their father began to swindle away, drinking and whoring his way into an early grave, meanwhile spending all of the family fortune trying to continue his lavish life. Before his death, he sold Grimmwald to the Hogge sisters; Kurt, angered deeply by his father's descent and the loss of the town, took Kopek and condemned the sisters beginning a life for the two as bandits, robbing and raiding on the road.

During this period, Kurt tried to keep his younger brother from seeing the horrors the men committed, such as rape or murder, though it still scarred Kopek deeply. Eventually, at a temple near Mirt, the gang assaulted a priestess, most likely of the cult of Coram Agh Tera, who cursed them all as she killed herself. A few days later, the group were turned into therianthropes: Kurt into a werewolf, and his brother a weredog. Kopek, hurt by this process, returned to Grimmwald to become a servant for the Hogges, and Kurt began buying elixirs from the witch at Crane Meadow to control his curse.

At some point afterward, the witcher Geralt of Rivia was hired by the Hogges to kill Kurt, though he was not told the full true story. Kurt, after a few days of the witcher's presence, attacked him in the town and convinced him to ask the Hogges who his true identity was to them. This resulted in Geralt believing Kurt innocent, then leaving the town to find Red with her arms torn up (actually by a doppler masking as a werewolf). This, combined with Lea Hogge being killed by Kopek in her sleep, meant blame for the two incidents was placed on Kurt.

entities.name: Lady Schwann
entities.description:
Lady Schwann was the wife of Joachim Schwann, the tax collector of Novigrad, and mother of their daughter.

After Joachim's death, she grew sour at her daughter's promiscuity and paid a mage to cast a spell that would teach her to save it for marriage: anyone she kissed would be transformed into a frog.

In , after folk spread word of a monster transforming daughters into frogs around the city, Lady Schwann was approached by the witcher Geralt of Rivia. She told him that her daughter had been tricked and kissed by the monster in the sewers. The witcher fought the creature, who told him Schwann's daughter was the actual one with the curse, and so Geralt confronted the two, convincing the mother and daughter to reconcile and reenlist the mage's help in removing the curse.

entities.name: Laurelnose
entities.description:
Laurelnose was an apothecary and member of the town council in Rinde with his eyes set on the mayor's position. Laurelnose's opinions about the state of the sorceress Yennefer's virtue earned him a public spanking from Geralt, which severely damaged Laurelnose's plans for the future.

entities.name: Lazare
entities.description:
Lazare was a close friend of the former baron of Creigiau, Anton the Elder, and was given the position of castellan and the hand of the baron's cousin, Éanna, as a reward for services rendered. The couple had one child, a son named Marcas. After his wife was killed, supposedly by a leshy, Lazare tried to go easy on his son, though he wished Marcas would take more of an interest in politics.

During the melee with the griffin at Creigiau Castle in , Lazare was taking bets for which knight would kill the creature. After Bryton de Creigiau killed it, Lazare told Geralt of Rivia to visit the castle's chapel in the morning. When the witcher got to the chapel, Lazare explained what had happened to Anton the Elder and his wife Éanna, while showing the witcher the tomb underneath the chapel.

entities.name: Lea Hogge
entities.description:
Lea Hogge was a Temerian woman and member of the wealthy and influential Hogge family.

At some point in the , the Hogge sisters worked with the Vivaldi Bank in Vizima and asked the bard Dandelion to write a song for the bank's founding anniversary when he came to visit. They eventually left the city and purchased Grimmwald from Karl Grimm due to its potential for tourism, and because they had funded the town knowing he would run out of money and sell it for dirt cheap. His son Kurt, after his father's subsequent death, was given six months by the sisters to regain the funds they paid to Karl, should he wish to buy back his family seat. People started to leave the town, believing the copper mine - Grimmwald's primary income source - to be dry and so the town doomed, in the process selling their houses for dirt cheap to the sisters. They began fixing up the town, opening fancy new shops, inns, and pubs, causing the rich to start flooding in. Kopek Grimm was enlisted as a servant, as well as Pioter, the local hunter. As a result, the cost of living rose dramatically, and so more original residents were forced to leave. Mama Ela with her namesake inn became one of the last to resist the sister's offers, especially after the recent arrival of a werewolf in the village.

In response to this lycanthrope, they posted notices for its death, which were answered soon after by the witcher Geralt of Rivia and his friend Dandelion. They contracted him to kill the beast, after denying the rumors they had hired it themselves. Geralt returned later with the knowledge the werewolf was in reality Kurt Grimm, and so the sisters explained the whole story of his family.

Throughout the night, Kopek, after ages of internal conflict between the Hogges and his brother, transformed into his weredog form and killed Lea. Her sisters found her in the morning, and with the help of a note with an inscribed location in her dead hands, the witcher, Dandelion, and Pioter headed off to Crane Meadow to find Kurt, as they believed him responsible.
entities.short_description: Lea Hogge was a Temerian woman and member of the wealthy and influential Hogge family.

entities.description:
Libushe (Polish: Libusze), or Libushka, was the wife of Caldemeyn (the alderman of Blaviken), and the mother of Marilka.

While her husband thoroughly enjoyed Geralt's company, Libushe didn't particularly like the witcher, believing he brought nothing but trouble. She also didn't like it very much when, on a past visit, Geralt tried to show off his witcher abilities by throwing a fork and killing a rat with it in complete darkness.

entities.name: Maerlina
entities.description:
Maerlina was a former midwife who later came to run her own bathhouse in Novigrad. She had a unique gift that, on top of aging slowly, allowed her to heal many different ailments and find pockets of healing springs.

Many years ago, she lived in Vizima and served as the first midwife to Queen Adda of Temeria, but was unfortunate enough to witness the stillborn and the death of Adda. The two were buried in the royal crypt and for seven years, life went on, until the stillborn awoke as a striga, terrorizing the palace and causing it to be abandoned and the staff scattering to the winds. For Maerlina, despite having had a tryst with the courtier, Ostrit, that resulted in a pregnancy and two children, she decided to set out into the world to find more honest work.

Using her abilities to find healing springs, she soon made a name for herself among numerous settlements while she wandered the world. Eventually she learned in passing that Ostrit had died 7 years after she'd left Vizima, though it was unclear of the exact circumstances surrounding his death, leaving her to believe he possibly absconded to Pont Vanis instead.

Eventually, the Third Northern War broke out so she sent her two children, Elisa and Elid, to stay with her mother in Velen, believing they'd be safer there. However, this didn't go as planned and when she finally reunited with her children, she'd learned they'd been cursed by misdeeds of theirs and the villagers': her son could take on the form of a crow and her daughter had turned into a monster with only one singular goal in mind: revenge. With this, her daughter chose to hide for the most part outside Novigrad while Maerlina setup a successful bathhouse in the city itself and proclaimed she only had one child: Elid, who wasn't that bright. Due to her son's new ability, she also had to constantly reprimand him to not spy on those who were nude, like in the bathhouse.

entities.name: Mama Ela
entities.description:
Mama Ela was a Temerian woman who lived in the town of Grimmwald. She owned her namesake tavern there, and was also the grandmother of Red.

Sometime in the presumed mid-, she purchased the tavern after the Grimm family constructed the town. Later, after it came under the control of the Hogge sisters, they offered her heavy sums for the property, wishing to complete control over Grimmwald's economy, though Ela never budged.

Eventually, a doppler, whose partner was killed by Pioter, found Ela, who gave him aid. After a bit of this relationship, she suddenly died or it killed her, burying her near her house and taking her form, so as to begin stealing change and profits from the tavern. This was thwarted weeks later, by the witcher Geralt of Rivia, after discovering Ela's grave.

entities.name: Manissa
entities.description:
Manissa was a witch in the service of Fregenal.

She was sent, disguised through illusion as an old woman, to ambush a druid sent by the Mayena Circle before they could discover the truth about Fregenal's experiments. She mistook the warrior Korin for the person sent by the Circle and attacked him, but was killed by Korin in self-defense. When the actual druid from the Circle, Visenna, appeared, she used necromancy to interrogate the dead Manissa. The corpse uttered the words "Fregenal", "Koshchey" and "treasure".

Manissa was the mother of Mousesack. Mousesack's father left Manissa when the future druid was still a small child. Mousesack unwittingly teamed up with his mother's killer. Not knowing that Korin had killed Manissa, the young Mousesack befriended him and Visenna, who took him to the druid circle in Mayena.

entities.name: Maraal
entities.description:
Maraal was the crown assassin of Maliq Nibras of Ofir.

In , Maraal escorted Dandelion to his quarters, where he met Dayo and Ameena. Later that night, when Dandelion was wandering the corridors, he nearly had another encounter with Maraal, just before Dayo hid him behind a curtain.

Later that day while Maraal was patrolling, he found Zaira lying down weak on the ground where she told him that a witcher had attacked her. Due to Maraal and her's secret relationship he attacked the witcher and was killed.

After his death, the rank of crown assassin was given to Erhan.

entities.name: Marcas
entities.description:
Marcas was the son of the castellan Lazare and his late wife Éanna.

According to his father, Marcas was more interested in women and drinking and showed little interest in politics. Around , he was acting as a squire to his second cousin and the baron of Creigiau, Bryton.

Geralt met him and his friend at the ruins outside of Creigiau Castle, while the witcher was hunting a leshy, but they were attacked by werecats. Marcas' friend was killed by the werecats, as was nearly the fate of Marcas, except Geralt saved him with Igni.

If neither of his second cousins, Bryton and Anton the Younger, produced an heir, Marcas was next in line to rule Creigiau. However since he, Anton, and Lazare died, the title of successor passed to Delwyn.

entities.name: Marta
entities.description:
Marta was a cursed human and Jakob Ornstine's wife before he killed her.

When Marta was 10, she would travel around her village and sell pastries, singing as she went, while being secretly followed by Jakob. As she grew older, Jakob fell in love with her, though she did not feel the same way. However, Marta's father sold her into marriage to Jakob for 21 silver coins and seven fox skins. Jakob was immediately abusive and would force himself upon her and beat her, all while telling her it was love. Marta also became aware that Jakob was inventing his own stories of them having a wonderful life together, a far cry from the reality.

Marta's only moments of peace were when she'd go collect seashells, as she saw them as telling the story of another world and wonderful lives elsewhere, free from the abuse she was going through. One day, Jakob destroyed some of her precious seashells as he wanted to have a new dagger created with them inlaid into the hilt. For this, he then sent Marta to put the order in with the blacksmith, Talton.

On arriving at the blacksmith's, the two immediately fell for each other and Marta began to frequently visit Talton under the pretense of checking on the dagger's progress, unaware that Jakob was getting suspicious. About three weeks into their affair, Jakob caught the two having a tryst on the beach and Jakob slaughtered Talton. However, Jakob fell into a further delusion and began to tell people Marta was instead attacked by a sea monster that nearly dragged her into the sea and the marks she bore were from it, instead of having been lover's marks left behind by Talton.

entities.name: Massy
entities.description:
Massy was a Nilfgaardian lieutenant who served in the company under the command of Captain Drugan. He was stationed alongside the captain and the rest of the company in the village of Vorune in No Man's Land. Whilst Drugan and his men were terrorising the hamlet and subjugating its residents, Massy appeared reluctant to take part. He was also far more accommodating than his superior when Geralt and Vesemir passed through the village during their search for Yennefer.

Later, he accompanied Drugan, the rest of the company and the two witchers during the hunt for the fiend that had been plaguing the local area. Perhaps in exchange for his earlier approachability and helpfulness, Geralt took Massy aside when the fiend was baited into attacking the captain and the rest of the company and Vesemir also saved the man's life when the creature turned on him.

A fight broke out, and Geralt left to go investigate.

entities.name: Mikula
entities.description:
Mikula was the master blacksmith in the smithy for the village of Klucz. Prior to becoming the village's blacksmith, he had served time in the military under the command of Voivode Grozim, and saw active duty in an unnamed war against the vrans.

When Klucz came under attack by the renegade druid Fregenal and his personal army, Koshchey's Men, Mikula sent for help from the druids' circle at Mayena. Whilst waiting for the arrival of aid, he called upon his past military experience to rally a small army of peasants from the villages of Klucz, Kaczan and Porog.

Mikula was one of the few brave enough to accompany Visenna and Korin on their mission to slay Fregenal's Koshchey, and was ultimately the one to bring the sorcerer himself to an end by beheading him with his axe.

entities.description:
Milda was a witch that resided in the Kestrel Mountains during the who assisted travelers and locals alike with her partner Zemyna with laments to heal their sorrow.

While teaching their current group of Giltine, Tulving, Kagan, Bandura, and two others, of the five stages of a lament: exordium, laudatio, comploratio, consolatio, and finally exhortatio, they were visited by the witcher Geralt of Rivia. He was looking for Giltine and after Bandura fought him to her death for her own exhortatio, he convinced Giltine to leave, though less than a day later he realised the retreat was the best place for her following her possession by a lamia, so the witcher returned Giltine to the two witches and left.

entities.name: Mouse Hunter
entities.description:
The witcher, mockingly referred to as "Mouse Hunter" and "Rat Snatcher" by Gweld and Geralt, was a member of the School of the Cat who participated in the Witcher Tournament.

When the Dyn Marv caravan passed through Kaedwen, "Mouse Hunter" was one of the witchers selected for a student exchange and the Witcher Tournament, as ordered by King Radowit II for the Schools of the Wolf and Cat.

On the day of the exchange, four witchers from the School of the Cat were supposed to be traded with an equal number from the School of the Wolf. However, when the Wolves arrived, only three Cat witchers were present. "Mouse Hunter" began to mock the Wolf witchers, insinuating that they were worth much less than their Cat counterparts. Offended, Gweld challenged "Mouse Hunter" to a duel, hurling mocking names like "Mouse Hunter" and "Rat Snatcher" at him. The duel quickly turned in Gweld's favor, as he was the more skilled swordsman. Just when it seemed "Mouse Hunter" would lose, a group of armed locals arrived. The Cat witchers falsely claimed that they had been attacked by the Wolves, and tensions nearly erupted into violence. However, Vesemir and Guxart intervened just in time to prevent a full-blown conflict. It was then decided that only Gweld would be exchanged, with the remaining witchers returning to their respective camps.

Back at the Cat camp, "Mouse Hunter" and the other Cat witchers secretly trained in wrestling, concealing their activities from Guxart and Gweld. Under the guidance of the king's astrologer, Astrogarus, they were preparing to betray the School of the Wolf during the tournament, intending to secure the royal funding and exclusive rights to operate in Kaedwen.

entities.description:
"Only ignorant fools belittle their significance."|citation = Geralt and Ermion, }} Mousesack (Polish: Myszowór), also known as Ermion, was a skilled and intelligent druid, and also a good friend and advisor to King Bran Tuirseach of Skellige, as well as Queen Calanthe of Cintra. He had a thickset and robust appearance and wore a bushy beard.

Even though the Mayena Circle was destroyed due to the plots of mages and kings, Mousesack and two older druids were invited by the king to a Witcher Tournament which was to take place in a special arena. When the tournament turned into a massacre of witchers of the Wolf School, Mousesack helped Geralt, his childhood friend, escape.

Mousesack was opposed to the arguments of Eltibald and Stregobor during a council of wizards in which he took part when they argued to consider the children born in the year of the Black Sun monsters.

Mousesack was present at the feast organized by Calanthe to celebrate Pavetta's coming of age, accompanying Eist Tuirseach and Crach an Craite as part of the delegation from Skellige. He communicated secretly with Geralt by manipulating breadcrumbs on their plates to form runes. Both men felt the impending trouble of that evening — Duny's return and Pavetta's power being unleashed — though neither knew the exact details beforehand.

Myrgot was a mounted Zerrikanian warrior.

Around the beginning of the s, Myrgot arrived in Caingorn with Borch Three Jackdaws and two fellow Zerrikanians, Téa and Véa. There, shortly before summoning people for a dragon-hunting expedition, King Niedamir organized a jousting tournament in which Myrgot took on the pious knight Eyck of Denesle.

After losing, Myrgot realized he put his country to shame and returned to Zerrikania.

entities.name: Myrgtabrakke
entities.description:
Myrgtabrakke was a female green dragon and the mate of the golden dragon Villentretenmerth. She became the target of a renowned dragon hunt.

Little is known about Myrgtabrakke's early life. She was active during the beginning of the 13th century. During that time, Myrgtabrakke mated with the golden dragon Villentretenmerth. Afterward, Villentretenmerth left her for the entire gestation period.

The dragon began her search for an optimal place for her nest, eventually finding it near the city of Barefield, within the kingdom of Caingorn. However, it didn't take long for the local villagers to notice her. They could not accept a dragon in their midst, so they decided to hunt her down. A villager named Sheepbagger prepared a poisonous mixture of hellebore, belladonna, hemlock, sulfur, pitch, and tacks, and he stuffed a dead sheep with it. Myrgtabrakke took the bait and devoured the sheep whole in one bite. She then tried to fly off but could not. Instead, she fell to the ground, barely alive.

Two of the villagers approached to confirm whether the dragon was truly dead. She killed them instantly but was so weakened that she could only lick their blood. After a while, she attempted to fly again but was simply too weak. Eventually, Myrgtabrakke limped away, clearly in agony. The locals saw that they had managed to gravely wound the dragon, but that was not enough for them as they wanted her dead.

entities.name: Niedamir
entities.description:
Niedamir, son of Audoen, was ruler of Caingorn and the first king of the Hengfors League. He originally ruled from the Royal Palace in Caingorn, but later moved his capital to the city of Hengfors.

In , when Niedamir was a young king, he participated in the hunt for the golden dragon, Villentretenmerth, and Gyllenstiern's employer. Niedamir joined the hunt due to his desire to conquer Malleore—after the sudden death of its prince, it was left in the hands of his daughter, a princess that the nobility of Malleore was trying to use to increase their power—a thing that would be rendered more difficult should she marry.

Niedamir had asked for her hand, but the nobles attempted to prevent any such union by using a conveniently discovered ancient prophecy which stated that the princess could only marry a man who had slain a dragon. Niedamir heard of the dragon of Barefield, Myrgtabrakke, and so set out on the hunt to slay her, thinking it a way to seize control of the principality while still conforming to the demands of the nobility.

Around the time of the First Northern War, he successfully seized control of Malleore and Creyden, forming the Hengfors League. At the end of the war, he signed the peace treaty with Nilfgaard, along with the other kings of the Northern Kingdoms. During this period, sometime after , the bard Dandelion went and joined his court in Hengfors, fleeing from the war.

entities.name: Nivellen
entities.description:
Nivellen was a cursed man who lived in Redania, in the woods near Murivel, in a secluded manor. He was called "Fanger" or "Degen" by the locals and stories of his "monstrous" nature were used to scare children. He was not considered a monster, due to being able touch to silver tableware and a witcher medallion without ill effects.

When he was a boy, Nivellen was quite sickly. His father and grandfather before him had made a fortune by leading a gang of highwaymen and cutthroats in order to steal from the local people, causing his father to be killed in an unfortunate encounter with a two-handed sword. Nivellen inherited command of the gang; initially, the enthusiasm and naïveté of youth banished any feelings of remorse and he participated willingly in the gang's misdeeds.

One day, the gang robbed a temple in Gelibol and coerced Nivellen into raping the young priestess there. Before killing herself, she spat in his face and cursed him, telling him that he was a "monster in a man's skin" and that he would become a "monster in a monster's skin". She also mentioned a way to lift the curse, but Nivellen didn't quite understand that part; only recalling her saying something about blood and a loved one. Unbeknownst to Nivellen and the gang, the woman was a priestess of Coram Agh Tera, the Lionhead Spider cult, meaning her curse was not an idle one.

Left alone in the manor, he resigned himself until one day he saw a man trying to steal roses from his aunt's garden. Enraged, he rushed outside to deal with the merchant, when he started to recall childhood fairy tales about princesses turning frogs into princes through true love, and so desperately lonely Nivellen demanded that the trader give him his daughter in exchange for his life, only to learn that she was too young as she was only 8 years old. However, feeling sorry for the state of the trader, Nivellen invited him inside his house and gifted him a small fortune as he had large reserves of money in his manor.

entities.name: Ostrit
entities.description:
Ostrit was a courtier in the court of King Foltest who loved the king's sister, Adda of Temeria.

Angered by the incestuous relationship between the king and his sister, and the pregnancy it led to, Ostrit cursed them, though it's unclear if it was him or the siblings' mother Sancia of Sodden (who also disapproved of the relationship) who ultimately caused the curse.

Both the mother and the girl-child died during the labor, and they were buried. Several years later, the curse bloomed and the girl rose as a striga, haunting the streets of Old Vizima.

Dissatisfied with Foltest's rule, Ostrit felt having the striga around would make it easier to undermine the king and have him overthrown. As such, when Geralt of Rivia was tasked to try and cure the striga, Ostrit tried to bribe the witcher into leaving the striga be. However, when Geralt refused, Ostrit threatened to kill him, only to be quickly knocked out by the witcher instead. Geralt then used Ostrit as bait to draw the striga out of its crypt, leading to the courtier's death a short time later.

entities.name: Paco Barbloes
entities.description:
Paco Barbloes was a nomadic mage likely hailing from outside the Northern Kingdoms that lived in the .

Whilst travelling through an unknown isle of Skellige, he happened upon the witcher Geralt of Rivia, a local woman Jula, her mother, and her warrior companion, all arguing over the morality and decision to kill the timid nekker also present. As Paco wished to obtain the creature's liver due to its psychoactive properties, he offered to commit the deed, though Geralt stood to protect it and Jula wanted it dead at her hand, so they all got locked into a standoff. This was broken moments later when the pig being held by the nekker suddenly squealed, causing Jula's companion to fire a crossbow bolt clean through Paco's throat, who, as he fell backward to the ground, responded with a fireball that hit and exploded Jula's head.

entities.name: Parlaghy
entities.description:
Parlaghy was a merchant and a member of the merchants' guild. When Xymena de Sepulveda, the daughter of industrialist Briana de Sepulveda, was kidnapped by an aguara, the entire merchants' guild clubbed together and funded an expedition to rescue the child. Alongside fellow merchant Kevenard van Vliet, Parlaghy offered his own participation and set out on van Vliet's cutter, the Prophet Lebioda, in pursuit.

Ultimately the rescue mission was botched, and instead of Xymena they managed to abduct a different she-fox altogether, prompting chase by its own aguara mother. Whilst guarding the she-fox, Parlaghy was thought to have inadvertently killed the girl, making flight from the pursuing vixen even more of a necessity. Nevertheless, the aguara caught up to the Prophet Lebioda and its crew, and when confronted by the creature, Parlaghy opted to jump overboard instead of face the consequences of his actions. He sank and drowned at once. Ironically, when the aguara met the witcher Geralt and minstrel Dandelion for the final time, she reveals that the 'death' of the she-fox was in fact an illusion, and that she was alive and well.

entities.name: Pioter
entities.description:
Pioter was a Temerian man that lived in Grimmwald, and was the primary servant to the Hogge sisters at their manor.

At some point while in service, two weeks after being attacked by a werewolf, he received the witcher Geralt of Rivia and his friend Dandelion at the gates of the manor, and after approval from the sisters, led them in. Geralt was charged with finding and killing the monster, and when he returned the night later, and revealed he thought there was validity in the creature's defense, Pioter went into a rage, screaming the monster had to die.

Again, Geralt returned later with the further knowledge the lycanthrope had been Kurt Grimm, who attacked Pioter out of anger at the sister's attempts to kill him and for "stealing" the town from his father. The witcher said he could no longer take the contract, as he thought Kurt docile and mentally scarred, and so left the town. Pioter found him and Dandelion, as well as Red and her grandmother soon after, however, when he went into the woods in a personal vendetta against Kurt. Red had been injured by the creature and said it was allied with the Hogges, which Pioter disagreed with, and so returned to the manor.

The following morning, Lea Hogge was found cut to pieces in her bed by her sisters and Pioter, clutching a note only writing "Crane Meadow". Geralt, Pioter, and Dandelion set off to the location, to find the witch that lived there. When they reached the snowy forests, they were attacked by a group of nekkers, which the three managed to fight off, Geralt gaining Pioter's respect for saving his life. Eventually, the three reached the witch's hut and Pioter sat with Dandelion talking whilst the witcher waited for Kurt with the witch. Kurt's arrival quickly angered Pioter and he shot a bolt into the creature's chest, who then turned into his werewolf form and began to attack, which caused both of them to become hindered in place by the witch's strong magic, who was furious at the spilled blood.

entities.name: Potrim
entities.description:
Potrim was a wealthy lord of Gelibol during the who was married to Juna, and whom received tributes from the local villages, such as Neisse.

After years of Potrim's incestuous rape of his young daughter Giltine, she fell pregnant with his child, though wishing not to keep it, asked her father for assistance. Potrim summoned a lamia working nearby to help terminate the birth, though not long after the creature went mad learning she had unknowingly supported their taboo relationship and was burned at the stake after she possessed women around Neisse to kill five men.

Later, after hearing a traveler tell Potrim of two women in the Kestrel Mountains who could relieve emotions, Giltine journeyed to them as she believed they could heal her intense depression following the death of her child and the abuse from her father. Juna began to lose her mind due to the disappearance of her daughter, wanting to commit suicide and randomly attacking Potrim. She was later saved from a group of water hags by the witcher Geralt of Rivia, and so Potrim's servant Agobard introduced the witcher to him. Potrim asked Geralt to rescue Giltine who he believed had been "taken" by the witches, which the witcher agreed to.

After Geralt returned with Giltine, Potrim and Juna became overjoyed greeting her before Juna seemingly out of nowhere bit her husband's nose, her mind still largely destroyed from the ordeal. Potrim and the witcher rode then to Neisse to celebrate in the inn, where Potrim bid him farewell after a quick discussion about the lamia. The lord rode home to find his daughter and wife; the former soon after attacked and killed him though by cutting his throat due to being possessed by the lamia haunting Neisse wanting revenge for involving her in their incestuous relationship.

entities.name: Radeyah
entities.description:
Radeyah was the crown sorceress to Malliq Nibras of Ofir.

Radeyah was acquainted with Yennefer of Vengerberg and at some point they fought each other aboard a ship at sea as Radeyah had stolen a rare magical artifact from Yennefer along with the mage she was sleeping with at the time.

Being a woman of great ambition, she desired to be the crown sorceress to the Malliq of Ofir, a post which at the time was held by the sorcerer Aamad. Fortunately for her, in Aamad was sent to the Northern Realms by the malliq to find the latter's missing son, Prince Sirvat. While Aamad did end up finding the son, he was too late as the cursed prince had just been slain by the witcher Geralt, who he tried to bring back to Ofir to be hold responsible but ultimately failed when the witcher managed to escape and killed the mage in the process.

At some point during the third Nothern War she went too the Northern Realms herself together with Ofieri mercenaries. While there she got into conflict with the Scoia'tael commando led by Vernossiel.

entities.name: Radowit II
entities.description:
Radowit II the Bold was a king of Kaedwen after the reign of Benda and before the rule of Henselt.

Radowit financed the two witcher schools active in his kingdom, Cat and Wolf, before or after the massacre of Kaer Morhen.

Persuaded by druids from Mayena and his court magician Astrogarus, he one day organized an ambush under the pretense of the Witcher Tournament which was supposed to compare the skills of witchers from rival schools. Astrogarus then promised the Cats monopoly on killing monsters within Kaedwen in exchange for attacking the Wolves during the tournament. However, just as the Cats were completing this task, Radowit ordered his soldiers to shoot all of the remaining witchers of both schools in the arena.

While the event did not bring about the absolute end of either of the schools as was planned, it drove a wedge between them and contributed to an already bad reputation of the Cats.
