entities.name: Codringher and Fenn
entities.description:
Codringher and Fenn was a famous law firm and detective agency in Dorian. It was founded by two men: Codringher and Fenn and had a reputation for getting the job done — for the right price. Their legal assistance was described to be somewhat dubious, because it often involved irrefutable cases being overturned through the sudden disappearing of evidence and witnesses suddenly redacting their testimonies or all-out vanishing.

For some time, Geralt of Rivia (and probably many others) assumed that Codringher and Fenn were one and the same person; that Fenn was simply another of Codringher's convenient aliases. But while Codringher did use other aliases, Fenn did in fact exist, though he rarely chose to be seen.

Around , they were approached by King Foltest of Temeria's spies who were searching for Ciri and Geralt. Protecting the witcher and his ward, he told them Ciri had died three years previous in a refugee camp in Angren of diphtheria, suffering before her death.

The following year, in June, they were informed by Dandelion of the mage Rience's escape in Oxenfurt, and later tasked by Geralt to learn what he could on Rience in the hopes of finding out what he wanted with Ciri. While most of the mage's background was missing, Codringher sold Geralt the information for 250 crowns, which did provide new insight into the mage's past before stating he could help the witcher make the problem disappear: to send a false Ciri that was of similar age and appearance as the real one, but the witcher refused. Codringher then promised to continue protecting Geralt, Ciri, and Yennefer's location if agents were to contact him. He also helped Geralt find out about Akerspaark's sons and thus uncovered a fraud.

entities.name: Coram Agh Tera
entities.description:
Some scholars stipulate that the Dauk and Wozgor religions contributed to the creation of the cult, as many of their beliefs are still instilled into it.

Coram Agh Tera is depicted in many forms. Some portray the deity as a monstrous spider hidden in darkness, while others describe an incomprehensible being existing beyond reality, weaving an enormous web that connects all living beings.

Followers of the Lionheaded Spider believe that Coram Agh Tera is the Great Weaver, an entity that creates and controls the threads of destiny. Human lives are seen as threads within its great web, constantly being woven, repaired, or cut. Sudden deaths are believed to occur when Coram Agh Tera breaks a person's thread.

The origins of the Cult of Coram Agh Tera remain uncertain. Some scholars believe that elements of the religion were influenced by older Dauk and Wozgor traditions, as traces of their beliefs can still be found within the cult.

entities.name: Council of Wizards
entities.description:
Council of Wizards, Supreme Council of Sorcerers, Council of Mages, or simply the Council, was the lower chamber within the Brotherhood of Sorcerers but still held considerable power among them and consisted of five members.

During the Thanedd coup, its members were split on all sides: Yennefer and Carduin remained neutral, Fercart sided with Nilfgaard, and Radcliffe and Philippa helped the North.

On June 30th , the Council and the Chapter of the Gift and the Art all assembled for the Grand Mage's Conclave on Thanedd Island, and socialized during the night before heading off to sleep. However the northern supporters, led by Philippa, who'd learned of the betrayal beforehand, stayed up and set their own plans into motion first, arresting all the Nilfgaardian supporters, like Vilgefortz, Terranova, and Francesca, before dawn.

When they were brought to Garstang to face a quick trial, Tissaia de Vries intervened on seeing her fellow Chapter members handcuffed and not getting a fair trial. Philippa explained their deceit but Tissaia also noted the northern supporters had acted similarly, revealing with an in-tranced Ciri the truth behind some of the north's actions. Wishing to remain neutral, Tissaia then removed the magic barrier around Garstang, hoping for a more civil outcome between the two sides. However, instead of a peaceful handling of the situation, the now freed Nilfgaardian supporters quickly began to attack the others and many were killed, both between the two sides and those who'd remained neutral. This coup resulted in the fall of the Chapter and Council, with many members fleeing north to the refuge of Redania, Kaedwen, Kovir, and Hengfors.

entities.name: Crinfrid Reavers
entities.description:
Originally they were only three - Kennet, Gar and their leader Boholt and they joined many hunts, like the one Myrgtabrakke, a dragon who lived outside Barefield, organized by King Niedamir. However, after Boholt lost his memory the remaining two beast hunters decided it would be wise to recruit. Around , they took a first apprentice called Newboy and a few years later they had entire bands of men like Jamor and Auwry, which they dispatched to countries as far as Toussaint.

The Crinfrid Reavers wiped out all of the dracolizards and forktails in Redania. They also killed three red dragons and one black dragon.

At some point, Geralt of Rivia and Yennefer were to hunt down the golden dragon, but were intercepted by the Crinfrid Reavers, who tied them up and decided to go after the beast themselves. They were not able best it, however, and were quite injured. Meanwhile, Geralt and Yennefer freed themselves from their bonds and moved on.

They raided a Melitele shrine and stole a now cursed talisman. Believing it to be good luck, they survived an encounter with a group of Scoia'tael warriors afterwards, when a dragon swooped in and attacked the elves.

entities.name: Crow Clan
entities.description:
The Crow Clan was an unorthodox druid group in Skellige led by the mysterious Crowmother. The clan members used crows as messengers, learning even their caw language while pushing their magic beyond what is normally considered safe.

The Crowmother is the Flaminika and founder of the clan. Her origins vary from being a cast out deity, powerful druid or relic, or even a crow in human form, however she has remained the clan's leader since its founding centuries ago. The clan see her as a maternal figure while outsiders see her as far more frightening due to her monstrous appearance.

They are a very secretive clan who rarely leave their home. When they do, traveling across the isles of Skellige or even across the Continent, they will only say they are being guided by either the Crowmother or crows in general. Despite this however they do still interact with non-clan members to acquire ingredients for their elixirs and to provide local communities with advice for their various needs.

The clan is on a quest for knowledge with crows being the key to obtaining the enlightenment they desire. Part of that belief is that, much like cats, crows can sense and absorb magic as well as peer into realms of reality beyond human perception. They hope to gain this enlightenment through communication with the birds and using their extensive alchemical knowledge to create Crow's Eye Rhizome. A toxic elixir that induces trances to help them communicate with birds. The effectiveness of this is unknown to outsides, although they claim it works.

The Free City also has a square near the Great Temple of the Eternal Fire named to honor a group of reformist electors who are credited with the city's rapid growth.

entities.name: Eternal Fire
entities.description:
Eternal Fire is a religious cult that had many followers among humans of the Northern Kingdoms. It was founded in Novigrad, where it was practically law, and the city served as the religion's de facto capital. The cult is led by an elected Hierarch, who's chosen by the Electoral College, with the seat currently being occupied by Cyrus Engelkind Hemmelfart.

The cult's greatest temple was the Novigradian Grand Picket.

By , the cult had grown in popularity to the point it was declared as the Church of the Eternal Fire. While it had no official acting army or military body, the Order of the Flaming Rose and witch hunters defended the Eternal Fire and upheld its laws, while the temple guards patrolled and protected the Grand Picket in Novigrad.

The Eternal Fire is one of the most influential religious movements of the Northern Kingdoms. Unlike many faiths of the Continent, it does not worship a god in the traditional sense. Instead, its scriptures describe the Eternal Fire as a divine force: the sacred flame that burns within the hearts of both mortals and gods, driving the eternal struggle against darkness and evil.

entities.name: Fallen Knight
entities.description:
The Imperial Secret Service had a plan to hire them and use them as a special force against Redania, much like they used the Scoia'tael in the first and second war, owing to the group's hatred of Radovid. However, this appeared to never come to fruition.

At the beginning of the war, Radovid had the Order sent to the front lines as mere "grunts" to support the Redanian effort to hold the Pontar while Radovid conquered Kaedwen. After they served their purpose though, Radovid took the Order's lands and confiscated all their money to finance his own war before formally disbanding the group. This caused the Order to split: those who didn't object to this were appointed as witch hunters while those that dared to stand up against the king were imprisoned or exiled. A small faction of the latter eventually made their way to the area surrounding Novigrad and Oxenfurt, now considered outcasts and filled with resentment towards Radovid.

With no land to call their own nor money to make ends meet, the Fallen Knights turned from protecting the downtrodden to taking advantage of them by selling fisstech, raiding merchant convoys, and shaking down locals for protection money. If anyone happened to stand in their way, such as fisstech competition in the area, they also had no qualms killing them off.

The Pacifiers were a famous group of mercenaries from the Nilfgaardian province of Gemmera, sent by Emhyr var Emreis, the emperor of Nilfgaard, to suppress the uprisings in the new conquests of the Empire.

In , they were deployed for the suppression of the rebellions in Ebbing, Geso and Maecht. Specifically, Thurn, a city in north Maecht, they sacked and burned to the ground.

entities.name: Geralt's company
entities.description:
Geralt's company (or hanza) consisted of Geralt, Dandelion, Milva, Cahir, Regis, and later, Angoulême.

The group had originally formed shortly after escaping Fort Armeria, despite Geralt's protests over Cahir and Regis joining. Through a variety of events and information, the group began to head south, to Riverdell, in hopes of finding the druids Regis mentioned that could help find Ciri. However, while in Riedbrune, Geralt was informed by the city's new governor, Fulko Artevelde, that the Nightingale gang had been hired by a then unknown half-elf to kill the witcher. Seeing a chance to take out the gang, Fulko, under no uncertain terms, asked Geralt to take care of it lest he inform his superiors what the group was really up to. As part of the deal though, Geralt asked to have Angoulême join him under the pretense of her being knowledgeable about the group, as she'd been with them before running away. However, this was also done to save her life, as the information she gave was only to buy her an easier, quicker death at Fulko's hands.

And so, as night fell and the rest were informed about the Nightingale gang, they declared once more they were a hanza, committed to finding and rescuing Ciri, or at least getting revenge if she was dead. However, by October the group reached Toussaint and Dandelion, having been a former paramour of Duchess Anna Henrietta, soon rekindled their relationship and decided he was going to stay in Beauclair. Their mission was also jeopardized by Fringilla Vigo, a visiting sorceress and the duchess' cousin, who took a liking to Geralt to keep him in Toussaint until May under the Lodge of Sorceresses' orders, as they had their own plans laid out for Ciri. This worked until early January, when it became clear that Geralt still loved Yennefer and, on overhearing a conversation, learned exactly where Vilgefortz's hideout was. In a last ditch effort, Fringilla wooed the witcher one last time before he left, getting him to reveal the location. However, having not trusted the sorceress, Geralt actually gave her a false location before leaving Toussaint with his company, sans Dandelion.

The company, riding through a blizzard in the various mountain passes, eventually made their way to Stygga Castle in Ebbing and began their assault. While it initially went well, with most of the mercenaries running away, they soon faced heavy opposition that resulted in Milva and a rival archer firing at each other simultaneously, mortally wounding each other. Shortly after, Angoulême and Cahir found Ciri, who was being pursued by Leo Bonhart and mercenaries, with one of the latter stabbing Angoulême in the thigh. Cahir stayed behind to fight Bonhart while the two women took off, but the knight was soon slain by the bounty hunter and Angoulême died soon after from too much blood loss. Meanwhile Regis went to help Yennefer and Geralt, who were pinned down by Vilgefortz, and while he managed to save Yennefer's life, Regis was torn apart and melted down by Vilgefortz.

entities.name: Great Sun
entities.description:
The inhabitants of the Northern Kingdoms know very little about the cult of the Great Sun. The head of this religion is a high priest, which may also be the Nilfgaardian Emperor.

The Great Sun, known in Nilfgaardian as Ard Feainn, is the dominant religion of the Nilfgaardian Empire and serves as its official state faith. Although today it is inseparable from the authority of the Empire, the cult was not always the central religion of Nilfgaard. For centuries it existed as one faith among many practiced in the imperial heartlands.

Its rise began during the reign of an emperor preceding Fergus var Emreis, who sought a unifying symbol capable of binding the Empire together more effectively than dynastic loyalty alone. Through political patronage, financial support, and legal reforms, the cult was elevated above all others. This process culminated in the March 8th Edict, which established the Great Sun as the Empire’s official religion and transformed much of its priesthood into an extension of the imperial administration.

The faith’s connection to the imperial family grew even stronger under the House of var Emreis. Earlier traditions claimed that Torres var Emreis, founder of the dynasty’s greatness, was the literal incarnation of the Sun and possessed a divine right to rule. Over time this belief softened into the doctrine that the imperial family is blessed by the Great Sun rather than descended from it, though some rural communities continue to preserve the older interpretation.

The most important and meritorious members obtain the secret sign of recognition: a star surrounded by flames, inscribed in a triangle, all golden.

entities.name: High Mountain Society of Sorceresses
entities.description:
The High Mountain Society of Sorceresses is a magical circle founded in the north of the Continent by a small group of sorceresses eager to recreate a stable arcane community far from the intrigues of the great royal courts. Established in the fortress of Highwatch, the organization pursues a dual goal: Restore a network of witch influence in the northern kingdoms and establish a cultural and social center where magic, politics, and prestige intersect.

The Society was born from a personal initiative of Louise van Adelaide, a former student of Aretuza, eager to recreate the community spirit and intellectual stimulation she had experienced during her training.

She was quickly joined by: Catrin Preece, main patron and social strategist. But also Clarisse de Claudine, reclusive alchemist of the mountains.

entities.name: Kingslayers
entities.description:
The Kingslayers, also known as Assassins of Kings, were an organization made up of a handful of witchers from the School of the Viper in the service of Nilfgaardian Imperator Emhyr var Emreis. The organization's task was to spread chaos in the kingdoms of the North by killing their kings with Letho of Gulet as the leader.

On the 25th of July, 1270 Letho was wounded by a Slyzard. Saved by Geralt he and two other Viper Witchers, Serrit and Auckes, would aid in Geralt's quest to rescue Yennefer of Vengerberg. After Geralt traded places with her in the Wild Hunt they took her into their care. They eventually made their way into Nilfgaard, where they arrested and given a mission by Vattier de Rideaux and the Imperator Emhyr var Emreis in exchange for freedom and the rebuilding of their School. The mission was to destabilize the Northern Kingdoms by assassinating monarchs. Letho agreed, gathered his comrades and traveling north.

Originally Letho planned Esterad Thyssen, king of Kovir and Poviss, to be the first victim but before he could act he was hired by Síle de Tansarville and Philippa Eilhart to assassinate Aedirnian King Demavend III. This was part of a conspiracy by the Lodge of Sorceresses to maintain control over the North.

On September 1270, a masked kingslayer entered to Royal Palace in Vizima and attempted to kill Foltest but the monarch was defended by Geralt. The assassin was eliminated and in the aftermath they uncovered he bore the cat-eye mutations of a witcher. He would be collected by the king's medics who would perform an autopsy. What remained a month later would be delivered to the mage Triss who could only determine he could see in the dark as good as Geralt and that his age was unclear, suggesting he was a witcher.

entities.name: Malatius and Grock Company
entities.description:
Malatius and Grock is a shipping company, operating barge deliveries between Foam and Novigrad on the Pontar Delta.

In , they hired Boatbug as a skipper on the barge, and for five years they completed successful trips, until , when they had to hire Geralt to travel on their barge because two weeks prior they had lost cargo and men to a mysterious monster. Six of Geralt's trips were completely without incident, until the seventh when they had trouble with fake Temerian guards looking for Geralt and Ciri. The trip ended in a successful delivery as the monster attacked the guards right in time.

entities.name: Order of the Flaming Rose
entities.description:
The Order of the Flaming Rose, sometimes simply The Order, is a religious knightly order established in with significant presence in the Nordling lands. At first, knights were mostly based and organized in the kingdoms of Aedirn and Temeria but later, after the uprising in Vizima, King Foltest confiscated the Order's assets in his dominion to finance repairs and they were forced to move further north to Redania and even Kaedwen.

The primary purposes of the Order are to defend the downtrodden from evil and spread the belief in the Eternal Fire, but they also serve as a police force or an iron fist to hunt down heretics. Before the death of the first Grand Master Jacques de Aldersberg, defending the needy extended to killing monsters for free as well but after reforms, they had less time to do that.

The Order of the Flaming Rose are mostly knights but the order also has foodmen and arbalester, they all work well together in formations. The Knights equipped with full body chain mail with armor with spikes and face helmet and long swords and kite shields, the order also as footmen are equipped with full body chain mail armor and helmet and sword and Heater shields, arbalester are equipped with chain mail shirt and leather armor and helmet and crossbow with arrows or fire arrows. The Order's commanders are equipped with full plate armor and chain mail and some use shields or not and twohanded sword, long axe, Spear or other weapons.

During the leadership of De Aldersberg, the coat of arms was a natural dark red rose in golden flames on a dark red field. Later the flame was changed to a ribbon and the rose was sometimes depicted as white.

entities.name: Order of the Golden Stirrup
entities.description:
Order of the Knights Stirrupers with the Arrow, popularly known as the Order of the Golden Stirrup or simply the Knights Stirrupers, is an old chivalric order tied to the Nordling goddess of horses and chivalry Epona. They recruit both women and men and while not as powerful as the Order of the Flaming Rose, the organization has a steady place in the Hengfors League.

The principal coat of arms used by the Knights Stirrupers is an amalgamation of two symbols: Cerbin of Emerida's family crest that had an arrow, and the golden stirrup used as a symbol by the original brotherhood.

The origins of the Order lie in the early centuries of Nordling forays. Starting as a motley brotherhood worshiping Epona, its members aided the knights in Toussaint and Cintra in prayer and with care for horses. Over time, the more pious of the knights decided to genuinely join the brotherhood. One such was the noble Cerbin of Emerida. Seeing the brotherhood's potential, he turned it into a chivalric order faithful to Epona.

The newfound order based itself in Cintra and, in accordance with local custom, accepted the members of both sexes in its ranks. The members are also allowed to intermarry, and their children are cared for by the Order. Upon reaching maturity, these children may choose between secular life and religious vows.

entities.name: Order of the White Rose
entities.description:
The Order of the White Rose was a knightly order active in the Northern Kingdoms, using several commanderies as their local strongholds. Easily identified by crimson cloaks with the emblem of the White Rose on their left shoulder, the knights were equipped with a helmet, armor-plated gauntlets, grooved breastplate, and carried a heavy sword. Those responsible for the Order's code, receiving of new members, and obtaining investitures from the aristocracy were gathered in the Chapter

Knights of the Rose were mostly nobly born gentlemen, even though later in the 1260s many sons of wealthy merchants, tailors, and burghers ended up joining the Order for a thousand Novigrad crowns. At this time many members of the Order, including Count Falwick of Moën, served Prince Hereward of Ellander, and thus gained a lot of influence and respect there, and a number of locals like Arthur Tailles joined in and took vows.

After the wars with the Nilfgaardian Empire and the death of Grand Master Rudolf Valaris, the order was dying and so a new charismatic leader, Jacques de Aldersberg, established a new order on the old, calling it the Order of the Flaming Rose. His aim was to protect the people from monsters and other evils, as well as to promote the belief in the Eternal Fire.

entities.name: Rangers
entities.description:
The Rangers, self-titled "Guardians of the Forest", are a group of volunteers who have as their mission "to hunt down and eradicate nonhumans". They enjoy nothing more than bragging about killing elves, spriggans, and dryads. Geralt and Dandelion are not very fond of them at all and while the witcher can keep his feelings to himself, the bard cannot. Dandelion taunted a table-full of rangers at a fair in Four Maples which ended up in an all-out brawl.

Luckily for Geralt and Dandelion, one of the bard's friends, a local alderman was able to intervene on their behalf and minimize the damage.

The Rangers may or may not be responsible for taking advantage of a mute red-haired girl found later among the wine casks out back with a rather silly smile plastered on her face and little else on.

entities.name: Terror Crew
entities.description:
The Terror Crew was a notorious and feared pirate fleet active in Skellige led by the infamous Morkvarg. The crew used to sail through the islands and raid every coast of the archipelago.

In , the crew met its demise during a raid at Freya's Garden in Hindarsfjall, where Morkvarg and his men destroyed the temple and murdered the priestesses. Before dying however, archpriestess Ulve was thought to have cursed Morkvarg, who suddently mutated into a werewolf and started devouring his own men. Only one member of the crew named Einar managed to escape from the garden.

In reality, however, the archpriestess had uttered no curse, and Einar, an ex-member of Morkvarg's crew, had been the one to curse him, through the use of a cursed pendant his father had given him.

entities.name: Yarpen Zigrin's company
entities.description:
Yarpen Zigrin's company were a group of dwarven mercenaries from Mahakam, who followed and supported Yarpen Zigrin. The group consisted of:

After the dragon hunt, Lucas Corto retired from the company to go live with his family in Mahakam.

In February , the company were transporting "special" cargo south through Kaedwen along the Lixela river, on the orders of King Henselt. Accompanied by Commissar Vilfrid Wenck who served Henselt, they made camp in the woods, and after a while, they were approached by Geralt, the mage Triss Merigold and the young girl Ciri, who they accommodated for several days along the trail, as Triss was very sick and needed to rest in their wagon.

The orders from Henselt turned out to be a test of loyalty, as Kaedwenian soldiers had already tipped the Scoia'tael to the company's location. The elven fighters ambushed the group, killing Vilfrid, Paulie, and Yannick. Furious at Henselt's deception, Yarpin condemned the king and continued south with his remaining men.

entities.name: Military ranks
entities.description:
In , there are many military units of varying kinds.

Ataman is a type of officer rank or title in the Redanian military. During his lifetime, Olgierd von Everec was ataman of the Redanian Free Company, also known as the "Wild Ones".

Captain is a military rank. A banner or a garrison is usually led by a captain. Generally the head of a non-military group (i.e. a gang of bandits) can be called captain as well. Captain is also the title usually given to the leader of the city guard.

A centurion is a non-commissioned officer (or NCO) similar to a Sergeant which commands 100 soldiers.
entities.short_description: In , there are many military units of varying kinds.

entities.name: Military units
entities.description:
Throughout The Witcher series, many different military units exist, sometimes changing names depending on the country.

A banner is a cavalry unit of 200 mounted men, led by a captain.

In the real world a banner was usually associated with a unit between 200-400 troops; it is possible that infantry banners exist and possibly fall on the upper end of the scale due to the comparative inexpensiveness of foot soldiers.

A division is a formation within an organized army or large military unit.

Led by the Field Marshal Menno Coehoorn himself, these forces were supposed to rip through the Northerner armies, end up behind enemy lines and then attack them from the rear. This effort proved ultimately futile as the inexperienced Poor Fucking Infantry, under the voivode Bronibor, was surprisingly able to thwart the Nilfgaardian cavalry advance and stand their ground despite the heavy casualties suffered. From this point on, Nilfgaard's defeat was inevitable and swift.

entities.name: Aedirnian Army
entities.description:
The Aedirnian Army is the military fighting force of the Kingdom of Aedirn. It is a professional army that is composed of knights, infantry, archers, crossbowmen, cavalry, and war machines. The most noteworthy and interesting unit of this army however, are the so called Aedirnian Special Forces - created by King Demavend III in as a direct answer to the threat imposed by Scoia'tael guerrillas. Recruits wanting to join this elite unit must undergo an unforgiving selection process, before receiving specialized training. As such, members of the unit are given an above average salary. They're divided into several sub-units, from which one was led by the infamous White Rayla. Half-elves were particularly welcome to enlist in the special forces.

Aside from ground forces and siege weapons like catapults or trebuchets, the Aedirnian military encompasses war galleys that are used to escort important figures, such as the Governor of Hagge or the King of Redania, along the Pontar river.

In , the Aedirnian Army defended Hagge from the invading Temerian Army, led by King Medell, and soundly defeated them, properly establishing the borders between Aedirn and Temeria.

In , during the First Northern War, the Aedirnian Army, along with the forces of Redania, Temeria, and Kaedwen, faced the invading Nilfgaardian Army in Lower Sodden, during the Battle of Sodden Hill. The northern armies were under the united leadership of King Vizimir II of Redania, and were successful in halting the Nilfgaardian advance.

entities.name: Aedirnian Special Forces
entities.description:
Aedirnian Special Forces was a group created in by King Demavend III of Aedirn to repel the newly-formed Scoia'tael.

While primarily seeking elite half-elf soldiers, enlisting in their ranks involved six months of training in brutal Aedirnian camps, and salaries payed equivalent to a soldier.

From , the forces led operations throughout the north, slaughtering or capturing the Scoia'tael, to face torture in town squares and an eventual end: crucified along the roadside. While generally supported in their actions, many soldiers faced some backlash for their brutal treatment of the nonhumans.

In June , Rayla and the four soldiers in her unit escorted Tissaia de Vries to Gors Velen for the Grand Mage's Conclave. At The Silver Heron inn, Rayla met with the sorceress and received permission for her and her unit to return home.

During the Second Nilfgaard War, it was led by Tibor Eggebracht. One of Tibor's subordinates was Devlin aep Meara. The unit fought at the Battle of Brenna, where Eggebracht was killed.

In , General Morvran Voorhis held the position of unit's commander.

entities.description:
The Blue Stripes was an elite Special Forces unit in the Temerian military. From , the unit was commanded by Vernon Roche, a former peasant that rose through the ranks to become one of King Foltest's most trusted military leaders. His second-in-command was Ves, a highly trained archer and arbalist.

The unit consisted of dauntless tattooed swashbucklers, interrogation specialists, noiseless scouts – all of them extremely loyal to their leader.

Unfortunately, during their stay at Henselt's side, the whole unit was accused for conspiracy and hanged on Dethmold's order.

After King Henselt's execution of the entire unit during the Third Lormark War, the unit was disbanded with Roche and Ves as its last members.

entities.name: Center Army Group
entities.description:
Center Army Group, also known as the Army Group 'Center', were Nilfgaardian troops during the Second Northern War under the command of Field marshal Menno Coehoorn. Its single most important task - to take Temeria, pushing the border of the empire as far north as the Pontar and hold that position. To accomplish this task, the support of two other flanking armed groups was required: the East Army Group and the Verden Operations Group. Of the two, the East Army Group had the more difficult mission. The original plan was unsuccessful, the Center Group being defeated at the Battle of Brenna.

The Center Army Group eventually ended up camped in southeastern Velen under command of Tavar Eggebracht and Field Marshal Havart var Moehoen during the times of The Witcher 3. It was either destroyed by the Redanian army under either Dijkstra or Radovid V or retreated back to Nilfgaard after the Temerians reclaimed their country as a vassal of the Nilfgaardian empire.

In , the Cintran Army faced the Nilfgaardian Army at the mouth of the Marnadal Stairs, in the Battle of Marnadal. Cintra suffered great losses and was defeated by the Nilfgaardians, and their king, Eist Tuirseach, killed.

Following the Sack of Cintra and the death of Queen Calanthe, the few soldiers remaining among the ranks either stayed faithful to their country and kept fighting under the command of Marshal Vissegerd, or deserted, in certain cases even by pledging obedience to Nilfgaard.

The City Guard of Vizima are the armed forces in charge of protecting the city and surrounding outskirts.

In , three members of the guard arrived to The Fox tavern upon hearing a fight, and found the witcher Geralt of Rivia, who was arrested and after using mind control to sway the guards, was led to Castellan Velerad.

Standard arms used by the guards include truncheons wound in leather straps and a sword. However, others are known to carry pikes and crossbows.

In , city guards are stationed at all gates and also roam the streets. They also help Geralt fight salamanders and other monsters if they happen to be nearby. Their default behavior is to help the witcher. They are based out of the city dungeon. The captain of the City Guard is Vincent Meis.

entities.description:
Deithwen ("white flame" in Elder Speech) was a division of lancers of the 3rd Nilfgaardian Army commanded by Colonel Liam aep Muir Moss. Both Deithwen and the heavy division, Ard Feainn, reported to Field marshal Coehoorn. The unit took part in the Battle of Brenna, where he charged together with the Ard Feainn Division on the right flank of the Northern army.

entities.name: Disgraced
entities.description:
The Disgraced were renegade Skelligers, so branded by the Clan Brokvar's Council of Elders, who were grouped and banished from the archipelago at some point in the first half of the 13th century.

In time, the Disgraced became known as near ideal mercenaries. Reasons were plenty: low cost, bearly ferociousness, no signs of fear or pain. They worked for many Continental armies. Nevertheless, after emerging alive from the battles – which they had been entering to seek death since the beginning – they often became frustrated and attacked regular soldiers. After stories of such incidents spread, only most desperate hired them.

In , they sailed into swamps of Angren where they encountered Queen Meve of Lyria and Rivia.

entities.name: Dun Banner
entities.description:
Dun Banner was a Kaedwenian light cavalry brigade from Ban Gleán and part of King Henselt's army. They were generally easy to recognize by their outfits which included cloaks and beaver hats.

They took part in the Battle of Brenna during the Second Nilfgaard War.

In early , a Dun Banner patrol warned and later saved Geralt of Rivia, Triss Merigold, Ciri and Yarpen Zigrin's company from the Scoia'tael hiding and attacking their soldiers in the woods. The Dun Banner had already known about the Scoia'tael attacking the company, as Henselt had organized it personally.

In July , after the fall of Aedirn in the Second Northern War, and Henselt's allegiance to Nilfgaard, the Dun Banner, along with five brigades, were sent to the Upper Aedirn, the long disputed land between the two kingdoms, to occupy. Three days later, they arrived and marched all the way up to the edge of the Dyfne river, prepared to meet the Nilfgaardian advance should tensions sour.

The Dun Tynne Guards were knights of Toussaint who served Lord Roderick at his castle, and its surroundings, along with mercenaries from Nazair. The captain of the guard was the lord himself, and the unit was almost entirely above the law. Most of the guards died when the castle was assaulted by the Ducal Guard led by Damien de la Tour.

Those who did not, either managed to escape somehow or ended up in prison shortly after the attack.

Henselt managed to halt the Nilfgaardians before they entered the Pontar valley, likely aided by Mahakaman maneuvers. The breakthrough came after the Battle of Brenna and the unexpected death of their commander, Ardal aep Dahy when the Northerners mounted a counter-attack. The combined armies of Aedirn and Kaedwen then proceeded to beat back the East Army Group, leading to clashes in the vicinity of Aldersberg. Ultimately, the Nilfgaardians lost and the Army was forced to retreat to the east.

entities.name: Faithel
entities.description:
The Faithel, outside Zerrikania mistaken sometimes with Free Warriors, are Zerrikanian female warriors who roam the Continent outside their native country in order to search for dragons and protect them from danger.

These of cule mailteini, that is teenage girls after 15, spend next 6 or more years in Faithel School on learning saberra swordmanship, sharpening their senses, and reflex conditioning. After finishing the school, every half a year they participate in the First Blood Tournament. Two best fighters receive a third belt of tattoo, are anointed by priestessess and blessed by the ruler, and set out outside the borders to look for dragons, venturing as far as the Dragon Mountains.

Faithel travel and fight in pairs. Their goal is to find a dragon, honour it and swear their allegiance, and, depending on the dragon's choice, escort it to Zerrikania or stay with it.

The name Faithel was first given to six warrioresses who accompanied Saulrenith and five other priestesses on their journey to Northern Kingdoms. The expedition, aim of which was to find dragons and spread their cult, met tragic climax 4 years after the beginning: after the news of the hunt for a green dragon in Mahakam reached them, Zerrikanians failed to protect the creature and only Saulrenith with three Faithel survived the fight with dwarves.

entities.name: Hyakki Yagyō
entities.description:
The Hyakki Yagyō, otherwise known as the Wild Hunt, or the "100 Oni Prowling the Night", are a ghastly retinue of specters led by Eredin Bréacc Glas that are known for kidnapping people with the help of yukinko, and incite great fear in the population of the Japanese-inspired land.

At some point, they kidnapped Ciri and took her beyond the Golden Bridge. Later, her father Geralt tracked them to Mount Kaijinzan, where he found and fought Eredin, who was assisted by yukinko. Eredin beat him down before the ronin escaped with the help of a nekomata, grabbing Ciri's sword off the specter in the process.

entities.name: Immortals
entities.description:
The Immortals were an elite armored unit within the Ofiri army. Their name was due to the fact that, whenever a soldier was killed off or seriously injured, he was immediately replaced by a new one, thus keeping the unit always full and strong. This immediate compensation for the injured and dead, combined with their near-impenetrable shield formations, made the Immortals a famously lethal force.

The Immortals cavalry, unlike regular mounted units, rode camels instead of horses, due to their better suitability to the desert. Their war chariots, complimented with three blades protruding from the wheels, easily sliced up the Ofiri's mounted enemies. However, the most fearsome combat asset of the Immortals was the war elephant, with their thick, leather skin that was often additionally armored, combined with saddle-platforms donned with archers shooting down hellfire. The soldiers equipment usually consisted of Ofiri armor, sabers, spears, shields, and bows. they also Wears red masks on their helmets, to cover their faces.

During the Third Northern War, a conspicuous number of Immortals, as well as war elephants, were sold to the Northern Kingdoms in order to fight against Nilfgaard.

The Impera was the imperial bodyguard brigade, charged with the personal safety of the Emperor of Nilfgaard. Never an empire to take this sort of thing lightly, the brigade numbered five thousand soldiers.

Commander Renuald aep Matsen is said to be previously a member.

There is a card with its name in Nilfgaardian Empire Gwent deck and also Impera Brigade armor.

As the oldest of the [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_Arms Combat Arms] they are the backbone of most armies. A soldier in the infantry is known as an infantryman. Infantry units have more physically demanding training than other branches of armies, and place a greater emphasis on fitness, physical strength and aggression.

entities.name: Iron Falcons
entities.description:
The Iron Falcons were a condottieri group formed some years after the Second Northern War. During King Radovid V's conquests, they were defying the royal authority.

To identify themselves they wore multicolored, flamboyant clothing and matching hats. Each member of the free company also fought with their own personal armory/weapon(s) of choice, leaving them extremely dissimilar overall in appearance. Generally, however, the infantry as expected wielded halberds.

entities.name: Jarl of Skellige's troop
entities.description:
The Jarl of Skellige's troop forms the main part of the Skelligan military. It is made up of dozens of hardy warriors who sail on the so-called drakkars, swift longships adapted for both the sea and river, under the command of the jarl of Skellige. The corsairs who serve in the troop come from all the isles, no matter the clan. Equipped with spears, swords, axes, and round shields, they often fight in a formation known as shield wall.

Usually consisting of 300 or so islanders, it would appear to be one of the weakest detachments on the Continent but their bravery, tactics, and renown had made them a force to be reckoned with. However, the troop cannot be considered a "proper army" as most of it is mustered during wars and then again dissolved. Instead of a regular army, each of the major jarls has his own unit loyal to him, while the king has an honor guard.

entities.name: Kaedwenian Army
entities.description:
Like many others countries in the Northern Realms, the kingdom of Kaedwen maintained a large and well-trained royal army, full of valorous commanders and brave soldiers able to tolerate the terribly cold weather of the terrain.

Although the Kaedwenian soldiers were not the best swordsman of the north, they were without a doubt the best in the use of siege weapons and cavalry units.

The "crème de la crème" of the Kaedwenian Army was the Dun Banner, a cavalry unit characterized by soldiers wearing beaver cloaks and caps. When the Nilfgaardian Army invaded the kingdom of Aedirn, the unit came to help their neighbors, succeeding in freeing the Upper Aedirn. Although King Henselt of Ard Carraigh considered his soldiers as "liberators", it was attested that the treatment reserved by the Kaedwenians to the inhabits of the Lormark was even worse than that of the Nilfgaardians. Later then, during the Peace of Cintra, the Lormark was returned to King Demavend III of Aedirn.

In , during the First Northern War, the Kaedwenian Army, along with the forces of Aedirn, Redania, and Temeria, faced the invading Nilfgaardian Army in Lower Sodden, during the Battle of Sodden Hill. The northern armies were under the united leadership of King Vizimir II of Redania, and were successful in halting the Nilfgaardian invasion. While many were lost in the battle, in the next couple of years, the defending soldiers left in Kaedwen were frequently attacked by Scoia'tael forces, and lost significant numbers, as well as Kaedwenian fortresses the army protected.

entities.name: Kerackian Army
entities.description: The Kerackian Army was the main armed force of the Kingdom of Kerack. Since the kingdom was located on the sea, the army's greatest power came from its fleet, which was one of the most notable among the Northern Kingdoms. Kerackian army frequently engaged in conflicts against the dryads of Brokilon, from which both parts suffered huge losses. During the Third Northern War, Kerack sent most of its garrison to aid Northern forces on the front lines. However, this left their defenses weakened and prone to raids by clans of Skellige. By the 16th century, the kingdom had been long gone, and so its army and its fleet.

entities.name: Landsknecht
entities.description:
Landsknechts are troops of colorful and dogged men, professional soldiers of fortune, whom cavalry can not frighten. Equipped with halberds, pikes, crossbows and double-handed swords that are roughly two yards long with hilt measuring two feet and large, curved cross guards they wake respect in many simpletons. Though predominantly of Temerian origins, they hail from and serve in armies of many Northern Kingdoms. According to Lambert, one of the Witcher fighting styles known as the strong style was devised by them.

Young Jarre and Melfi from Ellander met two Temerian Landsknechts on their way to the city of Vizima during the Second Northern War.

In the Temerian Army, they form elite infantry units, famous across the Continent. In contrast to other countries, where mostly commoners serve as foot soldiers, a number of noblemen can be found in the ranks of these regiments. They are organized in regiments under the command of captains appointed by the King. They rarely use armors, and if so, then only soldiers at the front with breastplates and helmets.

Landsknechts fight in the serried squares. Maintaining the rigid discipline is required. Each soldier is obliged to kill his comrade-in-arms if he sees him breaking out of formation. The Temerians move as one body striking by hundreds, or sometimes even by thousands, at once. The first ranks attack with 16-foot-long pikes. They are followed by the halberdiers, while the center of a square (where the commander and the banner are) is secured by warriors equipped with two-handed swords. The crossbowmen protect the sides of the formation.

entities.description:
The so-called Free Company was a cavalry unit created from all sort of bandits, renegades, mercenaries, soldiers and others normally considered outcasts in the Lyrian and Rivian Corps which consisted of the backbone of Queen Meve's forces during the second-half of the Second Northern War, after her previous army was completely annihilated during the First battle of Aldersberg. They terrorized the rear of the Nilfgaardian Army and looted their supplies, managing to persist until the end of the war.

Most of the unit's members belonged to the Strays of Spalla, led by Gascon while others were volunteers from Mahakam.

entities.name: Lyrian-Rivian Army
entities.description:
The Lyrian Army forms a professional military force of Lyria and Rivia, led by its monarch and select knighthood. It's a professional and valiant force, with quality full-plate armor and strong horses for its knights as well as adequate training and equipment for regulars though, in hard times, they recruit bandits, renegades, and other outlaws from Angren and Riverdell to expand its might as much as possible and start guerilla war in Dol Angra forests.

The army also doesn't refrain from taking in dwarves and donning them in white tunics decorated with red lozenges of Rivia. However probably the most notorious regiments consist of Lyrian Arbalests, who shot better than any other.

In the early morning of July 2nd , when the Second Nilfgaard War broke out, Queen Meve's forces were first to cross swords with the Nilfgaardian Army at Glevitzingen, Scala, and Spalla. In the beginning, the kingdoms of Aedirn and Lyria only managed to mobilize three thousand horse and ten thousand foot, of which one fifth had already been blockaded in the first days of the invasion, cut off in its forts and strongholds. Part of the remaining army had to withdraw to protect its flanks, threatened by far-reaching raids by light cavalry and diversionary strikes by Scoia'tael units. The remaining five or six thousand soldiers, including no more than twelve hundred knights, was unable to hold Rivia and so conjoined with Demavend III's army at Aldersberg. After Field Marshall Menno Coehoorn arrived with his remaining 13,000 men, including armoured companies, the Northerners were soundly defeated, leaving the two kingdoms to Nilfgaardian occupation.

Though Demavend was forced to flee to Redania, Queen Meve wasted no time and assembled a new partisan army, bravely leading partisans from the whole area as the "White Queen" into clashes like Battle for the Bridge on the Yaruga. After the Battle of Brenna, when the war turned against Nilfgaardian Empire her army got to liberate the domains along with Kaedweni Army and restored forces of Aedirn.

Magne Division was a division hailing from Magne, within the 4th Cavalry Army, Nilfgaardian mounted troops, commanded by Major General Markus Braibant.

When a Nilfgaardian cavalry officer steps out of line, he's likely to get reassigned to the Korath Desert. A few months patrolling the endless sands of this "frying pan" will purge him of any hint of insubordination, and replace it with frantic willingness to do absolutely anything to avoid being sent back.

entities.name: Mahakam Volunteer Army
entities.description:
The Mahakam Volunteer Army was a dwarven infantry unit. They were sent by Brouver Hoog to fight on the side of the Northern Kingdoms against the Nilfgaardian Empire. Due to them being non-humans, they were often sent on the most dangerous missions and to the most dangerous sectors, places that human commanders did not want to send humans to. They were armed with halberds, guisarmes, battle-axes, flails, and morning stars.

After having previously sent volunteers with Queen Meve's partisan army after a Scoia'tael attack in Mahakam, under strict orders that they were not to fraternise with humans and were to be sent back to the mountain realm after the war's end, he sent an army to aid the Northern monarchs when they launched their counteroffensives. The dwarves fought in Temeria down to the Yaruga.

After the Battle of Mayena, the regiment was recalled to Vizima to regroup and rest, as they had suffered heavy casualties. In Vizima, the positions that had become vacant due to deaths were filled, and many new volunteers joined after hearing news of the battle.

Having regrouped and rested, the dwarves then took part in the decisive Battle of Brenna. During the battle, they were positioned on the right flank and were 1000 dwarves strong. Following the victory at Brenna, they later also fought at Maribor and near the Yaruga.

entities.name: Nauzicaa Brigade
entities.description:
Nauzicaa (or Nausicaa), also known as the "Skullheads" or "Death's Heads", was a brigade of the 4th Cavalry Army, Nilfgaardian mounted troops commanded by Major general Markus Braibant. The brigade itself was commanded by Kees van Lo. They were equipped with war hammers and three and half feet long swords.

The Nauzicaa, together with the 7th Daerlan Brigade, were the last troops sent into battle in the battle of Brenna. Lead by the Field Marshal Menno Coehoorn himself, these forces were supposed to rip through the Northerner armies, end up behind enemy lines and then attack them from the rear. This effort proved ultimately futile as the inexperienced Poor Fucking Infantry, under the voivode Bronibor, was surprisingly able to thwart the Nilfgaardian cavalry's advance and stand their ground despite the heavy casualties suffered. From this point on, Nilfgaard's defeat was inevitable and swift.

entities.name: Nilfgaardian Army
entities.description:
The Imperial Army of the Nilfgaardian Empire is, without a doubt, one of the best-trained fighting forces on the Continent. Boasting from the lower ranks to the higher nobles involved within the military, its soldiers, known as the black-clad, are well-versed in the art of combat. Under the complete control of the Nilfgaardian Imperator who leads it through a set of high-ranking officers under a field marshal.

During greater conquests and invasions, such as the Northern Wars, the army was divided into groups, such as Center Army Group, East Army Group and Verden Operations Group. During the second of the Northern Wars, the army count was ca. 320,000, with 300,000 attacking the kingdoms and about 20,000 remaining in the Empire to keep the peace and defend core provinces in case of an unexpected turn in war.

Like many other armies, the Imperial Army is also in possession of siege weapons, including mangonels, trebuchets, Zerrikanian fire scorpions, and rot tossers.

Unlike the Northern Kingdoms, slavery is commonplace among the Nilfgaardians; slaves, usually prisoners of war, are used not only for manual work, but even during combat, fighting for their freedom, at least according to their masters.

entities.name: Poor Fucking Infantry
entities.description:
Poor Fucking Infantry, or PFI, was an infantry division consisting of conscripts and volunteers that lacked any relevant combat, riding, or archery experience. It was formed in Vizima during the war with Nilfgaard and it was there where Jarre and Melfi joined its ranks.

Every member of the division had tied a bundle of hay to their right leg and one of straw to their left one; The reason for this bizarre practice was since all the members were mostly illiterate and ignorant farmers who didn't discern the left from the right, for the sergeant who trained the unit only had to simply say "Straw, Hay, Straw..." instead of "Left, Right, Left..." during the marches.

The PFI took part in the Battle of Brenna under the command of the voivode Bronibor. Initially held in reserve, it was assigned to stop the counter-charge of the Nilfgaardian Nauzicaa and 7th Daerlan brigades. Consisting primarily of inexperienced pike-men matched against the enemy's cavalry the PFI sustained heavy casualties in the clash, Bronibor included. It did manifest a surprising valor however and managed to hold its ground.

The Infantry equipment included: Chain shirt, tabard, pike, helmet and dagger.

Redanian Free Company also known as Wild Ones, owing to the boar in their coat of arms, which was adopted from its leader's family symbol. They are an elite fighting unit consisting of experienced soldiers from aristocratic families, who were financed by Redania to support regular forces and the Royal Army during the Third Northern War.

They are fierce warriors fanatically devoted to their leader, but lack the discipline of the regular army. Their skills are as sharp as the blades of their sabers and definitely are not lagging in cavalry as well. As Olgierd himself said, in the bottom of their hearts they are common carousers and roughnecks good for a fight and drink, at least.

entities.name: Royal Redanian Army
entities.description:
The Royal Redanian Army was the core of the armed forces of the kingdom of Redania. They took part in the Second Northern War with Nilfgaard, during the battles at Brenna and Maribor.

In the battle of Brenna, the Redanian forces participating in the initial charge were led by Kobus, 9th Count de Ruyter. The rest of the Redanians were part of a hidden reinforcement, 10,000 horsemen strong, including in its ranks also Kaedwenian and Aedirnian troops. Under the leadership of General Blenheim Blenckert this force crushed the northern flank of the Nilfgaardians and turned the tide of the battle.

At the start of the Third Northern War, the army consisted of approximately 35,000 soldiers, including 4,000 mounted knights. The force was strengthened with the addition of Kaedweni and Temerian regiments, following the fall of the two realms to Redania and Nilfgaard, respectively. Koviri mercenary companies also allied themselves with the regular forces under the command of Radovid V to assist in repelling the numerically superior Nilfgaardian invasion force.

Around the 10th or 11th century, the Redanian Army, led by Marshall Milan Raupenneck, attacked the city of Loc Muinne, slaughtering the elven inhabitants. They then marched further to Est Haemlet and committed the same massacre against the elves there. This prelude led to a violent elven-human war; easily won by the Nordlings.

entities.name: Scoia'tael
entities.description:
Scoia'tael were nonhuman guerrillas also known as the Squirrels, due to the squirrel tails they wore on their hats/caps, the fact that they primarily lived in the forest, and the fact that they ate nuts.

Racism and deep-seated discrimination against nonhumans inflamed a great hatred of humans amongst nonhumans in the Northern Kingdoms. Most of the Squirrels were elves, however it wasn't uncommon to find halflings, dwarves (distinguished by their non-standard plaited beards), gnomes and half-elves among them. Scoia'tael were divided into commandos (considered to be a gnomish term) comprised of several fighters.

Bigger, more highly promoted commandos were rare and strictly established during battles or for special tasks (e.g. during the Thanedd coup). The most well-known Scoia'tael special tasks group was the Vrihedd Brigade, commanded by Isengrim Faoiltiarna. They were identified by their silver lightning bolt symbol.

Scoia'tael were allied with Nilfgaard and used by Emperor Emhyr var Emreis for diversion, as well as support for the Nilfgaardian Army during the Second Northern War. In exchange for their support, Emperor Emhyr var Emreis gave the elves Dol Blathanna as their own, independent state, and made Enid an Gleanna its queen. After the Peace of Cintra, they were condemned as outlaws even by their elven queen.

entities.name: Shevlov's free company
entities.description:
Shevlov's Free Company under Sergeant Shevlov's command was a law enforcement unit in Redania's service during the reign of King Vizimir II. The unit was tasked with enlarging the borders of Redania's Riverside province at the expense of those of the Temerian province Pontaria. Shevlov's Free Company liked to extort, harass and even burn down villages in the locality, despite being forbidden to do so by the king. Though their orders were to collect taxes, 'correct' the borders and drive opposing forces away, the company would also attack and sexually assault villagers whenever the mood took them.

During one excursion expanding the Redanian borders, they were ambushed by the mage Sorel Degerlund and his henchmen, including the hunchback Pastor and the giants, Bue and Bang. During this attack, most of Shevlov's Free Company, including Shevlov himself, were killed.

The "sly cats" were not anything like an organized group; the name was just used by King Esterad Thyssen for all the released prisoners, as a reference to a parable by which his wife, Queen Zuleyka, brought the idea to him.

entities.name: Temerian Army
entities.description:
The Temerian Army is the ground force of Temeria, forming its largest military component.

During its turbulent history, Temerian soldiers had crossed their weapons with many foes however mostly with the Royal Redanian Army, due to a rivalry between the two monarchies. Its core consisted of infantry units from cities like Vizima and Maribor as well as cold-blooded professional Landsknechts, whom cavalry could not frighten. Although generic foot soldiers usually drafted from villages and cities during times of war were in highest number, a goodly number of knights and influential nobles like Count Daniel Etcheverry of Garramone served in the army, often leading detachments.

Gathered under black flags aspersed with silver lilies, they also fought in Northern Wars. During the huge Battle of Brenna, 12 thousand brave Temerian and Redanian infantrymen formed the heart of Northern Kingdoms' might.

As is common in royal army contingents, Temeria utilizes several types of siege engine including trebuchets, catapults, ballistae, siege towers and battering rams.

In 1272, when Caleb Menge took over the secret service, the guard's equipment changed significantly. Members of the Guard were now fully armed and their colors changed to red and white. They also replaced lamias with steel swords and halberds. Some also had crossbows or bows.

entities.name: Toussaint Ducal Guard
entities.description:
Toussaint Ducal Guard is a force serving as both the police of Beauclair and vineyards as well as border guard in the small duchy within the Nilfgaardian Empire. Since the duchy is in constant peace with every realm and does not participate in conflicts between Nilfgaardians and Northern Kingdoms, the guard tend to fight just against bandit hanses side by side with Knights Errant. The only location that is not protected by this guard is Dun Tynne and surroundings, which is under the surveillance of the Dun Tynne Guard.

When it comes to the safety of important personalities, such as Duchess Anna Henrietta, or completing difficult missions, like for example the attack on Dun Tynne, then the Ducal Honor Guard (alternativelly Palace Guard) is summoned under direct command of its captain, which is Damien de la Tour in .

There are some variations regarding the guards' kit. The ones protecting the city are usually equipped with standard steel swords and halberds while the ones guarding vineyards are sometimes provided with military crossbows. Then there are also palace guardians with beautifully decorated long-swords, different halberds, crossbows and sometimes shields.

And after all, there is also a significant member of the guard, who serves as an executioner at the prison. Since this brute is a true professional, his weapon of choice is a double bit axe.

entities.name: Witch hunter
entities.description:
Witch Hunters were harsh, cruel, and fanatical members of an inquisitorial synod dedicated to the persecution and eradication of magic in Novigrad, Oxenfurt, and Velen during the witch hunts in . Equipped with swords, crossbows, dimeritium bombs, and shackles they were well prepared to fight both amateur and professional mages. They became even more formidable when the Order of the Flaming Rose was disbanded by Radovid V, resulting in some of the knights joining the witch hunters.

Though officially without any allegiance, their operations were sanctioned by the Church of the Eternal Fire and monarchs occasionally supported them with gold and firewood for the pyres. They were known as being intimidating as well as overzealous in their cause.

During this time, absolute loyalty and humility were required of sorcerers but some of them were accustomed to a different kind of treatment, thus this did not sit well with most of them. This, combined with one of Ithlinne's prophecies being wrongly interpreted, contributed to many deaths at the stakes and by torture, including several members of the Lodge of Sorceresses.

entities.name: Cianfanelli Bank
entities.description:
The Cianfanelli Bank is a dwarven financial institution owned by the namesake family, with branches across the Continent and beyond.

The first branch of the bank was founded by the ambitious Amadeus Cianfanelli when King Dezmod was still a snot-nosed brat. He did not stop at one branch and soon established locations in Kovir, Nazair, and even Zerrikania. His approach to customer service and handling their coin earned the bank significant renown.

Due to the success of the already established branches, more were opened, including those in Beauclair, Kaer Trolde, Ellander, and Novigrad. Most of their clientele were mages and monarchs, such as Foltest and Vizimir II, although the latter category tended to borrow more money than they deposited. Because of the city's economic importance, the Novigrad branch became the bank's main headquarters.

At some point, likely after the First Northern War, the mage Istredd came to the Novigrad branch on behalf of the Chapter to request coin. Unfortunately, due to Scoia'tael attacks, the bank mail en route from Gors Velen went missing. Nevertheless, a promissory note was issued, with the funds to be raised from the Chapter's stock market locations' turnover plus interest, with the money to be directed to the Ban Ard Academy.

entities.name: Confectioners' Mutual Savings Bank
entities.description:
The Confectioners' Mutual Savings Bank (Polish: Cukiernicza Kasa Pożyczkowa), also known as The Little Cake, is a Novigradian bank owned and run by halflings, with the president being the halfling Rulf Schoffeltom.

The bank was founded by four halflings and one human, all of whom were master confectioners. The bank's shareholders are mainly bakers and confectioners, with most of the bank's investments directed into those trades. Despite being a small bank, it is thriving. This is because the bank does not look down on those with limited financial means. Its clientele mainly consists of small merchants and craftsmen, cobblers, butchers, and market vendors, while also offering loans to the poorest with low interest rates and long repayment terms. There are also moderately wealthy citizens who use the bank's services, but most of the bank's profits come from countless small transactions, so many in fact that customers have to queue every day.

The bank itself is located in a modest wooden building with an upper floor and an attic. Upon entering the bank, there is a hall with a sleepy, grey-bearded, bald halfling with whom visitors must leave their weapons. On the ground floor there is the bank's pawnshop. Going upstairs leads into a huge hall where the bank's business is conducted. Pleasant, smiling female halflings in golden-brown dresses move about carrying trays of confectionery treats and cups of sweet juice. They politely ask clients the purpose of their visit, offer sweets, and guide them to the appropriate clerk. The bank is run exclusively by halflings, with only the security being dwarves and humans.

In four years, the bank made enough money for an impressive brick headquarters near the Western Bazaar, where finishing work is currently underway. According to rumours in the city, Vimme Vivaldi was alarmed by the bank's rising popularity and considered hiring arsonists to burn down the building, although nothing of the sort happened.

entities.name: Giancardi Bank
entities.description:
The Giancardi Bank is a financial institution with its main branch in Gors Velen, owned and operated by the dwarf Molnar of the Giancardi family, though other family-owned branches exist in Kerack, Novigrad, and Tretogor. The majority of staff are dwarves, though not all, and they are recognized by their identical uniforms.

Having existed since before the reign of King Dezmod, the bank's main headquarters were located in the city of Gors Velen, near the isle of Thanedd, home to both the Brotherhood of Sorcerers and the school of Aretuza. Due to its proximity to these institutions, the Giancardi Bank—especially its Gors Velen branch—maintained a close relationship with the mages. Through its main branch, many costly magical experiments were funded, along with the magic schools of Aretuza and Ban Ard Academy. Meanwhile, the Novigrad branch primarily focused on increasing the Chapter's profits by investing in the Exchange.

In and early , poll and winter billeting taxes levied by the military authorities were doubled. On top of that, every merchant or entrepreneur had to pay their "tenth groat" into the royal treasury. Non-humans also faced an increase in the poll and chimney tax and were additionally charged a compulsory donation of ten per hundred groats if they engaged in trade or manufacturing. Adding all that up, Molnar ended up paying sixty percent of his income into the treasury, and all the bank's branches spread over the Four Kingdoms contributed six hundred marks a year.

In June , Molnar, at Yennefer of Vengerberg's request, made a 1,500 oren donation to the Temple of Melitele in Ellander, an anonymous 2,000 Novigradian crown payment to the school of Aretuza for Ciri's tuition, and asked for three hundred crowns in cash. Instead, Molnar provided a banker's draft for five hundred. He also offered to cancel a debt worth 100 crowns incurred by Geralt in Dorian, but Yennefer objected and instead proposed that he raise the payment for Geralt's contract in Hirundum.

Gibellini and Son is a relatively young dwarven bank, founded by the aging dwarf Yazon Gibellini and his son.

According to urban legend, the pair came to Novigrad with Yazon having only a single crown. They managed to build a financial empire in the city, with their bank being situated in the Western Bazaar. The bank's employees are dwarves. Father and son are ruthless in their dealings, exploiting the smallest loopholes in contracts as well as mercilessly enforcing debt. While it has not been proven, there is a lot of talk of the bank having connections to the city's criminal underworld, linking it to extortion, arson, and even murder.

Around the time of the Northern Wars, it opened a branch in Novigrad, though despite their attractive terms, people were reluctant to use its services, believing it to be an extension of the Nilfgaardian Military Intelligence, as well as accusing it of handling the Scoia'tael's money.

entities.name: Redanian Post Bank
entities.description:
The Redanian Post Bank (Polish: Redánski Bank Pocztowy) is a state-owned bank from Redania. Its headquarters are located in Tretogor, and its solvency is guaranteed by the Treasury of Redania.

Redania had an excellent royal courier service, alongside which a state-run Horse Post was established. These transported letters and parcels to all major Redanian cities, as well as several major foreign cities. As they began transporting money on a larger scale, the kingdom introduced postal bills of exchange. At the largest post offices, proper banking houses were established where one could exchange bills for cash and cash for bills. Under the initiative of Sigismund Dijkstra, these were reorganised into a proper banking network.

Its branch in Novigrad is located next to the city's exchange. On the ground floor there is a branch of the Redanian Horse Post; following the broad white marble stairs leads one into the bank's offices. There, beneath a large Redanian eagle, stands a large desk where an official sits alongside bank clerks. The official provides clients with all necessary banking information, while one of the clerks escorts them to the appropriate door. All banking business is conducted in private offices. The bank enjoys popularity among circles hostile to non-humans and the dwarven monopoly on banking. Much of its clientele consists of aristocrats, famous sorcerers, and representatives of wealthy merchant companies, and especially in Novigrad, supporters of the unification of Novigrad with Redania.

entities.name: Vivaldi Bank
entities.description:
The Vivaldi Bank was founded by the Vivaldi family. Through their hard work, it became one of the Continent's most powerful banks.

The Vivaldi bank was already operating well before the human kingdoms had their first kings. Through the Vivaldi family's hard work, their bank became one of the two most powerful banks on the entire Continent. The bank's headquarters were located at their branch in Novigrad, but they established many other branches. They set up branches in all the larger cities in the North, and to oversee this vast network, they had key branches that oversaw specific regions. The Pont Vanis branch oversaw Kovir, Poviss, Caingorn, and Creyden. The Tretogor branch oversaw Redania and Kaedwen. The Vengerberg branch oversaw Aedirn, Lyria, and Sodden, and the Vizima branch oversaw Temeria and neighboring countries. Vimme Vivaldi carried the torch for his generation, making the Novigrad branch of the bank the largest bank in the city.

In early , the Vivaldi bank informed Molnar Giancardi that several attempts had been made to track the correspondence of the sorceress Yennefer of Vengerberg. The branch in Vengerberg also discovered an attempt by a disloyal clerk to track all transactions of her private accounts. Vivaldi either didn't or couldn't investigate the case, and the disloyal clerk ended up drowned in a ditch. They also informed Molnar of this.

The branch in Vizima encountered some financial difficulties, which led to a hostile takeover of the branch by humans, leaving the bank director Golan Vivaldi poor and bitter. The bank was used to pay the bail money for the criminal known as the Professor. The bank would eventually return to the family's control when the Scoia'tael under the command of Yaevinn stole documents that allowed Golan to regain control. After regaining control, Golan sent someone to check on the profitability of a mine in Vergen.

entities.name: Zammorto Bank
entities.description:
The Zammorto Bank is the smallest of the dwarven banks in Novigrad, but its position is unquestioned. It is owned and run by the Zammorto family.

The Zammorto Bank was founded in the city of Novigrad. There, it competed with other dwarven banks such as the Vivaldi, Cianfanelli, and Giancardi banks. Although the Zammorto Bank is the smallest of the dwarven banks, it nonetheless holds an undisputable position in the city's financial system. Traditionally, the bank's president, Gabron Zammorto, heads the Guild of Bankers.

Furthermore, the Zammorto Bank is practically the only one that does not engage in commodity trading on the exchange. Its source of income lies in its activity on the credit market. The low interest rates on loans ensure that they always have many clients — from small business owners to members of the ruling classes. On June 15, 1260, the bank issued a promissory note of 10,000 crowns for the firm Reihrin, Crammer and Reihrin.

The gang's revenue came mostly from thefts, pickpockets, and extortions. Their headquarters was located in the Putrid Grove.

They also had some affairs in Oxenfurt: the main Cyprian Wiley's mansion was indeed located there.

entities.name: Gang
entities.description:
Gangs or "Hanza" (from the Nilfgaardian term "aen hanse") tend to be para-military, criminal or mercenary groups, usually bound by familial ties, friendship or a common goal. There are several such examples on the Continent:

During the Third Northern War, four large criminal syndicates were active in Novigrad, sharing power with Church of the Eternal Fire. Their leaders were Francis "The King of Beggars" Bedlam, Cyprian "Whoreson Junior" Wiley, Sigi Reuven (alias used by Sigismund Dijkstra) and dwarf Carlo Varese. To citizens, these leaders were known as the Big Four and balance existed.

Things changed when Cyprian allied himself with King Radovid V of Redania who provided him with intelligence and finances. In return, the king wanted Whoreson to kill the other three underworld heads. Later, when he was of no use for the Redanian king the latter betrayed his location to Geralt of Rivia who had a personal score to settle with Whoreson.

After Whoreson's fall, many criminals attempted to take advantage of the dysfunction in a power grab. Among these criminals were Duke and Earl.

Hegel preferred to fight with a heavy blunt axe.

Manfred preferred to fight with a sword.

entities.name: Michelet brothers
entities.description:
The Michelet brothers were professional murderers for hire in the Redania area.

Toublanc was the "brains" of the operation, being the only one to attend temple school, and therefore the de facto leader, while the other three brothers were the "brawn".

In early , while in hiding from their contract issued by the mayor, the three were introduced by Vilgefortz to the mage Rience, who hired them to attack an "ordinary man" for 100 crowns. Realizing something was off, Toublanc demanded 200, which Rience readily agreed to. The brothers and Rience went off to Oxenfurt after the man, Geralt, and during the fight quickly realized he was a witcher.

After Geralt incapacitated the four brothers, Philippa painlessly finished off Toublanc with a stiletto, ending the line of Michelet.

The Nightingale gang was led by Homer Straggen (also known as Nightingale). They were insolent, cunning and cruel and so, very serious about their business. They were admitted to the imperial service and hired by Schirrú to kill Geralt.

The gang was destroyed in Caed Myrkvid and almost all of its members, including their leader, were killed either by the knights-errant of Toussaint or by the Caed Myrkvid druids who burned them alive.

entities.name: Nissir
entities.description:
The Nissir were Baron Lutz's of Tyffi's militia that were stationed near the border of Geso. The gang, referred to as "the minions of the law" by the baron, were known for raping women and killing cattle, which greatly contributed to the fear they inspired in Nilfgaardian citizens. The leader of the gang was Vercta.

In July , Baron Lutz ordered the Nissir to capture the Rats, another gang. In particular, they captured Kayleigh and were in the process of bringing him back to Tyffi to be punished for robbing one of Lutz's administrators. While stopping at the inn in Glyswen, they met up with Vercta's friend, Skomlik, the leader of the Trappers, and together they coordinated their respective gangs' efforts.

It was at this inn that Ciri, the Trapper's prisoner, helped Kayleigh escape by taking a knife from the innkeeper and cutting his bonds. Then Vercta's whole group and the Trappers were slaughtered by the Rats, who showed up to rescue Kayleigh.
