entities.name: Pinto gang
entities.description:
The Pinto gang was a group of robbers and horse thieves commanded by Pinto.

In August , whilst in Loredo, a village in Geso, they encountered the fellow gang known as the Rats. The Pinto-allied tall man with a mustache made sexual jokes about two of their members, Ciri and Mistle, whilst his fellow gang members applauded and chanted. When he tried to harass them sexually, Ciri killed him, in a flash cutting his throat with two strokes of her sword. Giselher, the ringleader of the Rats, interceded before another member was killed. Scornfully, he paid Pinto one thaler by the pound for the dead bandit.
entities.short_description: The Pinto gang was a group of robbers and horse thieves commanded by Pinto.

entities.name: Rats
entities.description:
The Rats (Polish: Szczury) was a young gang of criminals in Geso that were known for stealing from the rich to satisfy their own material wants, which included having the best horses, clothing, and accessories.

However, their lust for murder soon caught up with them and their overconfidence caused them to take on a legendary bounty hunter, resulting in their deaths.

Each member came from a different troubled background. Kayleigh's village had been ransacked by Nilfgaardian forces. One such soldier was Reef, whose comrades had left behind due to his injuries. Despite this, both 16-year-olds joined forces and killed and robbed a tax collector. Giselher had deserted from an unknown army and joined a gang in the area, but they were unlucky enough to stumble into a free elf territory and most were killed by their arrows. Giselher was pinned to a tree by one but was then rescued by the elf Aenyeweddien, better known as Iskra, who'd been banished by her people, meaning almost certain death for herself if she traveled alone. Mistle came from a wealthy, noble family but their town was forced to flee from approaching "pacifiers". Having been pampered since childhood, she couldn't keep up with fugitives and wandered alone until manhunters found her, intending to sell her and the other young girls off. However, they were attacked by a gang who then raped all the women, including Mistle. After being left for dead, she was found by Asse, who'd been following that gang for revenge on what they did to his own family.

All 3 groups ended up meeting during the Festival of the Harvest in Geso, being drawn to each other due to their shared interests in fancy outfits and horses but also what they had all recently been through thanks to the rebellions. They then took on the official name of Rats after someone referred to them as such, and which they all liked.
entities.short_description: The Rats (Polish: Szczury) was a young gang of criminals in Geso that were known for stealing from the rich to satisfy their own material wants, which included having the best horses, clothing, and accessories.

The band was dismembered (quite literally) after they stood in Geralt of Rivia's way in the town as they meant to take the market goers hostage if the mage Stregobor didn't come out of his tower to face Renfri.

entities.name: Salamandra
entities.description:
Salamandra was a criminal organization led by a Zerrikanian sorcerer named Azar Javed active throughout the Northern Kingdoms, particularly in Temeria with their main base and hideouts in its capital city of Vizima. The origin of this group is unknown, though one could find ordinary lackeys, trained assassins as well as renegade mages among their ranks.

Members of the organization wore a symbol depicting a salamander, the fire lizard, usually tattooed on their head, but sometimes elsewhere.

In May , a large contingent of Salamanders attacked Kaer Morhen, the Witchers' Fortress, and stole the secrets of the mutagenic substances and stimulants, so closely guarded by the School of the Wolf for hundreds of years. With these in hand, the group began to create a number of mutants in the hopes of creating a "perfect mutant".

When they started to create mutants at first they experimented with animals and this produce a very powerful mutants before moving onto experimenting on humans, although with mixed results.

entities.name: Stefan Skellen's gang
entities.description:
Stefan Skellen's gang consisted of various mercenaries, thieves, and bandits from across the region. While the purpose was for Stefan Skellen to hunt down and capture Ciri on Emperor Emhyr var Emreis' orders, this wasn't relayed to most of the gang members, only that they were looking for a certain girl.

Members of the gang were recruited by Dacre Silifant, Ola Harsheim and Bert Brigden and they were then brought on the 14 September at Rocayne, where Stefan Skellen was waiting. Unbeknownst to Skellen, there were two traitors among his group: Neratin Ceka, having been planted by Skellen's boss Vattier de Rideaux, and Jediah Mekesser, who was a spy for the sorceress Assire var Anahid.

The first task of the gang was to investigate on what Leo Bonhart did after he slaughtered the Rats with the exception of Falka in Jealousy: Nycklar, a young boy hired to Bonhart to deliver some letter, was captured from Malhoun and was brought to Rocayne, where Stefan Skellen interrogated him; it turned out that the letters Nyclar delivered were addressed to Esterhazy of Fano and to Dominik Bombastus Houvenaghel of Claremont.

On 16 September Boreas Mun, Neratin Ceka, Chloe Stitz, Andres Vierny, Cyprian Fripp, Dede Vargas and Joanna Selborne went to Fano and interrogated Esterhazy, the local weaponsmith. Esterhazy told them that Bonhart and Ciri were here four days before and that Bonhart bought a sword for Ciri.

entities.name: Strays of Spalla
entities.description:
The bandit group formed after the revolt in dungeons of Spalla Castle and mainly consisted of pickpockets, racketeers, cutthroats, and assassins. Armed with slings, daggers, instruments of torture stolen from Spalla (headman's axes, saws, hammers), they were known to be cleverer and bolder than common bandits: they attacked heavily armed convoys and noblemen's mansions.

In , while Queen Meve was attending a meeting with the other monarchs of the Northern Kingdoms, the Strays took advantage of her absence and attacked Hawkesburn, where the tax collectors' offices were located: all the gold got stolen.

Meve, returning from Hagge, started tracking down the Strays until she finally found them at Lord Clayton's residence. There, after learning about Clayton's death, Meve finally met with the Strays leader: one Gascon. After a intense battle, Lyrian troops defeated the Strays and captured Gascon, who was later brought to the capital in order to be executed.

Once arrived at the capital however, Queen Meve was overthrown by Count Caldwell and by her son Villem, who planned to surrender the country to Nilfgaard and confined Meve to the castle tower. It turned out in the end that the Strays were just a distraction planned by Caldwell for Meve in order to gain time and secretly treat with the Empire.

entities.name: Syanna's Gang
entities.description:
Syanna's Gang was a gang based out of Nazair that had formed sometime prior to .

When Syanna was still a teenager, she was cast out of her homeland of Toussaint and left for dead on the edges of Caed Dhu. As luck would have it though, some of the gang was camping in the area and when the former princess found them, instead of hurting her, they took her and took her back to their home in Nazair, where Syanna joined their gang and quickly rose through the ranks before eventually leading them herself.

Like a typical gang, they took part in the usual criminal activity like stealing, fencing, and killing, but with her thoughts still on Toussaint, Syanna eventually decided it was time to return around 1275 and make those who hurt her all those years ago pay for their misdeeds.

Syanna used the group to do her bidding and blackmailed her former lover, Dettlaff, into killing the four knights that had escorted her out of the duchy as a teenager. She also used some of the men to barter for Sangreal wine and to try and steal back the Heart of Toussaint, both of which she believed to be her birthright. However, the latter item turned out to be the group's undoing as it pinpointed her as the mastermind behind all the killings. The group was eventually massacred during a combined attack by Geralt, the Toussaint Ducal Guard, Regis, and Dettlaff on Dun Tynne Castle.

entities.name: Syndicate
entities.description:
Before the Syndicate was formed around late or early , Novigrad's underworld was best described as a chaotic battleground between various gangs, agents of foreign intelligences, dwarven banksters, law enforcers and religious militias. Such a chaos used to cause problems for the commercial centre of the North and posed a potential danger of being abused by the Nilfgaardian Empire, whose army was supposed to inevitably attack again.

Being aware of the current situation's drawbacks, Count Sigismund Dijkstra from Redanian Secret Service (under the alias of Sigi Reuven) initiated the birth of the Syndicate at meetings with the city's hierarch, Cyrus Engelkind Hemmelfart, and leaders of the four most influential Novigradian gangs: Carlo Varese, Cyprian Wiley, Francis Bedlam, and Gudrun Bjornsdottir. Although the meetings were originally spent mostly on disputing the spheres of influence within the city, the final agreement was eventually reached.

Dijkstra/Reuven returned to Novigrad at some point between 1268 and from his exile, and finished the Syndicate's Code of Conduct. The organization was joined by two large traders in the fisstech market: Azar Javed, the leader of the Salamandra, and Jacques de Aldersberg, Grandmaster of the Order of the Flaming Rose

The relationship between gangs in the formative years of the Syndicate was apparently fluid, as by 1272 the Tidecloaks no longer controlled the city's port. The four most influential leaders, known as the Big Four, plotted against each other and against the hierarch, disagreeing at topics such as the situation of the sorceresses or the exact areas of the city to control. After Cyprian "Whoreson Junior" Wiley accepted Radovid V's money and attempted at assassinating the other three members of the Big Four, his gang was nearly obliterated by Carlo's Crownsplitters and he found himself betrayed by Radovid who gave the information on his hiding to Geralt.

entities.name: Trappers
entities.description:
The Trappers were a gang of trackers and slavers, led by Skomlik, who were tasked by the prefect of Amarillo to capture Ciri. The expedition was actually led by a Nilfgaardian knight, Sir Sweers, but the latter did not survive the return trip.

In July , the Trappers under Sweers' orders were scouring the western borders of the Korath desert for Ciri when they found her unconscious upon the bank of the Suchak river. A few days into their return with her, in the moorlands of Geso, they were stopped by the members of the House of Varnhagen, which resulted in Sweers fighting and dying, meanwhile killing both of his opponents. Ciri then attempted to escape, though she was captured and thrown at Skomlik's feet, who had just become de facto leader. He called over his brother-in-law Remiz, who had been a servent of the Varnhagen's, and invited him into the group, then reiterating she would be taken to Amarillo for the bounty.

Afterward they stopped in the village of Glyswen and met up with a fellow gang, the Nissir, at the inn. Skomlik, being old friends serving with their leader Vercta, was boisterous in his attempts to convince the Nissir to give up their captive Kayleigh to Amarillo or the local villagers, though Vercta explained their reward awaiting them in Tyffi. Seconds after Ciri and Kayleigh managed to get free from their restraints, thanks to a knife from the innkeeper, the Rats broke through the door and attacked the two groups, killing them all.

entities.name: Zoltan Chivay's company
entities.description:
When the Second Northern War erupted, the dwarves Zoltan Chivay, Munro Bruys, Caleb Stratton, Yazon Varda and Figgis Merluzzo, along with a gnome named Percival Schuttenbach and a green parrot named Field Marshal Windbag, formed a company to escape from the enemy front and reach Sodden, passing through the Turlough Hills, the river Chotla and the Ina. During their trip, they met some refugees from Kernow (only women and children), and they decided to help them and travel with them.

Later, the gang met with Geralt, Dandelion, and Milva, who were traveling to the south toward Nilfgaard, in order to find Ciri in the City of Golden Towers. Although Zoltan Chivay and his mates remained very stunned by their suicidal intentions, they decided to travel together to the Ina, since the route was more or less the same.

On the Ina, the company was attacked by Nilfgaardian soldiers of the 7th Daerlan Brigade and parted with Geralt and the others. While trying to escape, Caleb Stratton remained killed and was then buried by his mates under a birch. Some weeks later, Geralt, Milva, Dandelion, Regis and Cahir Mawr Dyffryn aep Ceallach, who recently joined Geralt's company, met again with the dwarves near Ysgith in Angren.

In the end, Geralt's company and the dwarves decided to part: Zoltan told Geralt that he and his mates were returning to Mahakam, so he gave his Sihil go the witcher as a gift. Before definitely separating, Zoltan revealed that in Dillingen they robbed and probably killed an old and rich Havekar and buried his goods near the "O" river, which they planned one day to collect.

entities.name: Aretuza
entities.description:
Aretuza was a magical academy for young ladies situated next to Garstang palace on Thanedd Island, that was founded by Klara Larissa de Winter It consisted of five floors and seventy-six rooms, including rooms for the students. Among the students were girls from the twelve finest families in Redania.

The central hall was built in a "T" shape, and the long side had narrow and extremely tall stained-glass windows which cost a small fortune, reaching almost to the top of the columns that supported the ceiling. The ceiling was so high it could be difficult to make out the frescoes decorating it, mainly nude statues. The many candles throughout the hall were kept alive with magic, so as to be not affected by the slight drought that could be felt. The Gallery of Glory found in the palace displays artefacts from throughout the history of magic.

The annual fees for a student added up to 1,200 Novigradian crowns, with a 200 crown matriculation fee for new students. Adepts studying there were not permitted to leave the island, were forced to abstain from sex, and visitors were only admitted to the lowest level of the academy, Loxia.

In June , Vilgefortz summoned a Grand Mage's Conclave to be held on the island, many of the students having been moved away to Loxia beforehand to make room for the visiting mages. On the last night of the month, they met in the palace for a banquet. Throughout the night, a large-scale coup took place between the mages allied with the North and those with Nilfgaard, resulting in numerous mages being killed or captured, such as rector Tissaia de Vries who committed suicide, ultimately spelling the end of the Brotherhood.

entities.name: Ban Ard Academy
entities.description:
Ban Ard Academy, otherwise called Ban Ard Sorcerer's School or Ban Ard School, is a prestigious university educating male students in magic, as well as one of the two main seats of Brotherhood of Sorcerers since the fall of Mirthe during Falka's rebellion. Located in Kaedwen, just outside the city walls of Ban Ard which the Academy also owns, its facilities are placed in what used to be an Aen Seidhe palace.

Though the school has an exceptional education system, people like Margarita Laux-Antille may consider its female counterpart, Aretuza, to be more highly esteemed due to its students having better results during comparisons.

The first organized school of magic that trained both sorcerers and sorceresses was located at Mirthe, and was followed by a school for girls founded by Klara Larissa de Winter in Aretuza on Thanedd Island. which was at that point the capital of Kaedwen. In , King Dagread moved the capital to Ard Carraigh, closer to the geographical center of the Kingdom, and granted the whole Ban Ard to the Academy. Following the scorching of Mirthe by Falka's troops, the surviving male staff of Mirthe moved to Ban Ard around the 1150s.

By , the position of the Chancellor of the Academy had been held by the venerable Euclides Croft.

entities.name: Gweison Haul
entities.description:
Gweison Haul was the state magical academy of Vicovaro but now serves as one of the Empires most prestigious magic academies second only to the Imperial Magic Academy and it is the place most mages in the Empire go to in order to study the arcane arts. The Empire shipped enemy mage's laboratories and studies back from the lands it conquered. Because of this the furniture and architecture of the academy has become somewhat eclectic.

Little is known of Gweison Haul's origins, though it has long served as one of the foremost institutions for magical education. Over the years, it has developed a reputation for producing disciplined and capable practitioners of Cham, placing safety and control above displays of raw power.

The academy's philosophy was shaped by the dangers inherent to magical practice. Numerous examples of magical accidents, injuries, and rogue practitioners have reinforced the belief that power without restraint is a threat both to the mage and to those around them. As a result, Gweison Haul's curriculum emphasizes concentration, emotional regulation, and gradual progression rather than the pursuit of increasingly spectacular feats.

The presence of Mage Hunters within the academy further reflects this history. These agents are empowered to respond to magical threats arising within the institution and serve as a constant reminder of the consequences of losing control.

entities.name: Imperial Academy
entities.description:
Imperial Academy is a Nilfgaardian university and the main academic rival for the University of Oxenfurt. Located in Castell Graupian, it was known mainly for its departments of humanities and science. It also produced many linguists and translators. The academy did not have a department of military science; for that, there was a separate military academy in the city of Nilfgaard.

Many Nilfgaardian legends, chronicles of the their kingdoms, and genealogies of their kings are kept at the academy, as well as most of their writings.

In the mid 13th century, members of the academy, led by Professor Noel Ivor, began local archeological expeditions, aided by shipments of goods from Castell Graupian.

Years later, Ivor and his assistant Philipp Borutt, left on an eight week expedition to the Termes Palace Ruins in Beauclair, on the hunt for Isabelle Duchamp, a fellow scholar who was from the Oxenfurt Academy, gone missing at the ruins. Only a couple days after arriving however, on the 18th of Birke, Ivor was killed by wraiths when he entered the cursed palace.

entities.name: Imperial Magic Academy
entities.description:
Like in many others countries of the Continent, even the Nilfgaardian Empire owns a Magic Academy where mages are taught. Emhyr var Emreis, Imperator of Nilfgaard, hired many mages in his court from this school. While the academy is located near Loc Grim, another academy is located in Vicovaro.

While the vast majority of students pass through Gweison Hall, the more prestigious children of the Empire are sometimes extended the opportunity to study at the Imperial Magic Academy. This royal academy was created to train the highest echelon of Nilfgaard's magical community. The students of the Imperial Magic Academy are not as stricly controlled as the students of Gweison Haul. In almost all case the students who graduate from the Imperial Magic Academy can join the army as adjudants, acting as advisors or are employed by their family.

Some students of marginal abilites from wealthy families may be admitted to the Imperial Magic Academy after an appropriate contribution to the school.

Each student receives a lavish personal room and the school is staffed by servants who are at the student beck and call. During the holidays, the Academy hosts feasts and celebrations on par with those of the capital.

entities.name: Markus Braibant Military Academy
entities.description:
Markus Braibant Military Academy is situated in Nilfgaard, the capital city of the Nilfgaardian Empire. Here, the members of the noblest families of the Empire are trained to become officers in the Imperial Army. It is named after Major general Markus Braibant, who served in the Imperial Army until , when he was killed during the Battle of Brenna. One of the Academy's mottos was "War to the palaces, peace to the huts"; during the Northern Wars however, the last part of the motto was totally forgotten.

entities.name: Witcher schools
entities.description:
The witcher schools are the organizations which train and equip witchers, the itinerant monster slayers. While schools differ in mindset and details of training, most of their differences still equate equally proficient hunters. Headquartered in secluded locations, each one is built on the blood, sweat, and tears of countless children who stood within them, honing their technique and skill.

Split off from the original Order of Witchers, created in the , the schools continued to train new generations of witchers. Most of them had fallen up to the first half of the under various human attacks, but at least some of them were rebuilt and continued to function even in the .

entities.description:
The Aedirnian Special Service, or Aldersberg Corps, is the intelligence agency of Aedirn, primarily based in the Old Citadel of Aldersberg.

After King Demavend III met with the northern rulers at Hagge in , spies from the service heard news of the mage Rience tracking Ciri, the princess of Cintra who was orphaned in the capital's slaughter. Believing that Nilfgaard was attempting to capture the girl, they began a continent wide search to hunt down and kill the princess, so Aedirn could partially decide Cintra's future.

entities.name: Kaedwenian intelligence
entities.description:
The intelligence agency of Kaedwen is primarily based in the capital, Ard Carraigh.

While taking enlistment, they primarily picked out individuals with great potential, such as exiled mages and spies.

In the , during the reign of King Henselt, recruitment officers from the Kaedwenian Secret Service found the mage Rience outside Ban Ard Academy, having been kicked out for thievery. They enlisted him and trained him as a killer, before he left to pursue greater things.

After Henselt met with the other northern rulers at Hagge in , spies from the service heard news of Rience tracking Ciri, the princess of Cintra who was orphaned in the capital's slaughter. Believing that Nilfgaard was attempting to capture the girl, they began a continent wide search to hunt down and kill the Princess, so Kaedwen could partially decide Cintra's future.

entities.name: Nilfgaardian Military Intelligence
entities.description:
The Nilfgaardian or Imperial Military Intelligence is the Nilfgaardian Empire's intelligence agency but, despite being the largest country on the continent, it's only the second-largest intelligence agency next to the renowned and efficient Redanian Secret Service.

Ever patient in its goals, Nilfgaard carried out several long-term missions within the Northern forces themselves, such as with Gwalter aep Llwynog, an imperial spy sent by General Ardal aep Dahy. Using the alias Xavier Lemmens, he joined Aedirn's forces stationed in the city of Rosberg several years before the actual war. While he managed to keep his real loyalties a secret, he was caught just as he was trying to carry out his orders to kill Queen Meve.

During the sack of Cintra, Cahir Mawr Dyffryn aep Ceallach failed to bring Princess Cirilla to the imperial court, and Stefan Skellen was then tasked with finding, capturing, and bringing Ciri and Cahir to Emperor Emhyr var Emreis. To achieve this, he formed a band of various mercenaries and also hired Leo Bonhart, a famous bounty hunter. They organized the Scoia'tael attack on the mages' conference on Thanedd Island.

Spymaster Vattier de Rideaux and his network of agents were handed a crushing defeat which was orchestrated by Sigismund Dijkstra at the beginning of the Second Northern War with Nilfgaard.

entities.description:
Novigrad Security Bureau is an intelligence network of Novigrad directly subordinate to the Church of the Eternal Fire. It's headed by the Minister for Security Affairs, hierarch's éminence grise and the most powerful person in the city, and has an armed hand in the Temple Guard.

Since Novigrad lies so close to Redania and its capital Tretogor, the Free City's spies and guards often cooperate with the Redanian Intelligence.

entities.name: Redanian Secret Service
entities.description:
Redanian Secret Service is one of the finest intelligence agencies in the known world (next to the Nilfgaardian and Koviri intelligence agencies).

They lease quarters on the top floor above the vice-chancellor's offices at Oxenfurt's Academy, which Sigismund Dijkstra liked to call the "Faculty of Most Contemporary History", while Dandelion liked to call it the "Faculty of Comparative Spying and Applied Sabotage".

Within Redania, the secret service was generally loathed and feared - mainly because of their reputation for frequent executions of those deemed to be traitors and spies, even though the vast majority of them indeed were spies and traitors.

In , Dijsktra enlisted Dandelion into the service, and asked for a report on the situation with King Ervyll in Verden. A year later, after returning to Oxenfurt, Dijsktra wanted information about Geralt of Rivia, whose location Dandelion protected with a lie.

entities.name: Temeria's Intelligence Service
entities.description:
Temeria's Intelligence Service is the intelligence agency of Temeria, mainly based in the city of Vizima.

Expanded greatly by King Foltest in the 13th century, they were responsible for the capture of wanted peoples, delivering messages, and transferring news of the war.

At some point in , agents of the Intelligence Service infiltrated Aedirnian Special Forces stationed in Aldersberg, and made an unsuccessful attempt on the life of underage Prince Demavend III, an act meant to be Medell's revenge for the shameful defeat Virfuril handed him near Hagge.

In , after Foltest met with the other northern rulers at Hagge, spies from the service heard news of the mage Rience tracking Ciri, the princess of Cintra who was orphaned in the capital's slaughter. Believing that Nilfgaard was attempting to capture the girl, they began a continent wide search to hunt down and kill her as that stopped Nilfgaard's control of succession. Later during the search, they approached the "lawyer" Codringher in Dorian for advice, who falsely told them Ciri had died in Angren to throw them off her tail.
